articles.title: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Bank measures can only limit damage from ‘digital arrest’ scams

Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s exasperation, during the Supreme Court’s hearing on October 29 on the “digital arrest” scams, that people still fall for such scams despite abundant warnings and orders from the Court is understandable. About ₹800 crore has been lost to these scams this year even after recoveries, a hefty sum from the savings of individual victims. But this is not merely about gullibility. Scammers posing as CBI or police officers succeed because their victims, older citizens in particular, defer to or fear law enforcement. When Indian police are widely seen as high-handed towards ordinary citizens and as serving only the powerful, the threat of an “arrest” over a video call cannot be that implausible for many. That said, the Court’s pressing of the Reserve Bank of India to finalise its KYC Amendment Directions, 2026, which require banks to flag suspected mule accounts and put temporary debit holds on them, is welcome. CBI investigations have shown that mule accounts are central to scammers laundering their proceeds after duping victims and that bank staff have, in some cases, helped open them. With the availability of complete transaction histories and AI tools, banks can now spot anomalous transactions faster. The Attorney-General’s assurance that the directions will be in force by December 31 is also welcome. The Court’s insistence that banks compensate victims addresses an issue with the RBI’s zero-liability provisions. Its 2017 circular covers only unauthorised transactions, leaving victims who were coerced into making transfers without any recourse.

Yet, full compensation for the victims whenever banks are found wanting in due diligence must be implemented with care as this might force banks to flag far more than the actual mule accounts. Already the RBI directions cast a wide net. Any transaction of ₹1,000 or more that is ‘unusual’ for an account holder’s declared profile, or linked to a reported account, can be held for up to 60 days, and longer if directed by the police. In cases where small traders and Jan Dhan account holders have unknowingly received transfers from mule accounts, freezing their accounts for two months or more is a disproportionate penalty. Also, the Court’s suggestion that unusual transactions must be automatically reported to the police and physically verified raises privacy concerns. These measures must ensure that genuine account holders are not penalised for bank failures. Many of these scams are run from compounds using trafficked Indians in conflict-ridden parts of Myanmar and in Cambodia and Laos where they have thrived due to some degree of official patronage. India must use its clout to pressure these regimes.
Editorial Context: Beyond gullibility: On digital arrest scams. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Social security concerns of unorganised sector workers remain

One year after the implementation of the Code on Social Security , the Union Labour Ministry has constituted the National Social Security Boards for Unorganised Workers and Gig and Platform Workers. The constitution of the boards, though delayed, is a welcome step. However, the highly centralised nature of this mechanism may hinder its optimal outcomes. By design, the Union Government controls both the Boards: they will be chaired by Union Minister for Labour Mansukh Mandaviya. The Board for Unorganised Sector Workers will have 40 members, nominated by the Union Government. They include seven members representing unorganised sector workers and seven members representing employers of the unorganised sector. Similarly, the Board for the welfare of gig and platform workers will have 22 members with five representatives each from the aggregators and the workers. But they have no significant representation of Central Trade Unions from the Opposition side or from the State Governments ruled by the Opposition. Labour is in the Concurrent List of the Constitution and both the States and the Union must work together to improve the living standards of workers.

The International Labour Organization defines social security as the ‘protection that a society provides to individuals and households to ensure access to health care and to guarantee income security, particularly in cases of old age, unemployment, sickness, invalidity, work injury, maternity or loss of a breadwinner’. The Union Government claims that the country’s social security coverage has increased from 19% in 2015 to 64.3% in 2025, which is around 94 crore citizens. However, it is apparent that the unorganised and gig and platform workers, who make up more than 92% of the country’s total workforce, are far from enjoying any social security under this definition. Almost two decades ago, the National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector, headed by economist Arjun Sengupta, recommended a slew of measures to improve the social security of workers in the informal sector. The issues raised by the panel still remain unaddressed. A report prepared by Justice V. Gopala Gowda for the Keralam Government in March this year flagged certain anti-federal and anti-worker characteristics in the Social Security Code and suggested amendments. The Union Government should take the trade unions and the State Governments on board while creating new systems and mechanisms to address the social security concerns of the vast majority of workers.

Editorial Context: Suboptimal outcomes: On social security boards for unorganised, gig, platform workers. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Public functionaries must not use privacy to seek exemption from scrutiny

The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.
• The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has pointed to the SIR’s flaws by design

At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Clinging on: On Netanyahu and the Israel elections
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Netanyahu’s continuance will be bad news for Israel and the region

Benjamin Netanyahu was at the centre of Israel’s October 27 elections. For Israel’s longest-serving Prime Minister, who oversaw a genocidal war in Gaza following Hamas’s October 7 attack , the election was the biggest test of his political career. For the Opposition, which promised to hold him accountable for the failures of October 7 and end the country’s “forever wars”, the election offered an opportunity to oust him from power. The results, however, sent a mixed message. With 85.6% of the votes counted, Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition has lost its majority but is still the largest bloc . His Likud party is projected to win 26 seats, while its main rival Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, is expected to secure 21. Otzma Yehudit and Religious Zionism, the far-right extremist parties in Mr. Netanyahu’s coalition, demonstrated their continued strength, winning 13 seats between them. The dark horse, however, could be the Arab parties — the Joint List is projected to win 12 seats while the United Arab List (Ra’am) could secure seven seats. With neither bloc commanding a majority, the Arab parties could propel the opposition coalition to power. But the big question is whether the anti-Netanyahu coalition is ready to join hands with the Arab parties, which have historically been kept on the margins of Israel’ s power politics.

Mr. Netanyahu’s central promise has been that only he can guarantee Israel’s security. Yet, the October 7 attack took place on his watch and he has refused to take responsibility for the failures that led to it. A wanted man by the International Criminal Court, he has repeated, before and after October 7, that a Palestine state would not be formed while he is in power. His war on Gaza has killed over 70,000 Palestinians, including 20,000 children, and displaced the region’s population. Israel’s brutal occupation machinery has also expanded and tightened its control of the West Bank, while settler terrorists have unleashed violence on Palestinian households. His war on Iran has been a disaster, with global economic consequences. Mr. Netanyahu has sought to portray his wars as bold, necessary moves to protect Israel, while exploiting Israelis’ security concerns for political gain. He may not be voted out immediately, but his failure to secure a majority and the decline in his party’s popularity are significant. The Opposition should take its cue from the results and form a broad coalition with the Arab parties. It should restore accountability in governance, revisit his unchecked militarism and rebuild ties with the world. If Mr. Netanyahu continues to cling to power, it would be bad news for Israel and the region.

articles.title: Hunker down: On Cyclone Arnab, its landfall
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Proactive governance kept the casualties low after Cyclone Arnab

Cyclone Arnab, the first named storm of the North Indian Ocean cyclone season this year, intensified rapidly before making landfall as a ‘very severe cyclonic storm’ on October 28. This particular rapidity is a challenge for forecasters and some models did fail to anticipate how strong Arnab would become. It also moved faster than expected towards the coast, before stalling for a time and beginning the landfall process several hours before the India Meteorological Department (IMD) had predicted it would, in the middle of the night, leaving many district authorities with a potentially narrower window to evacuate high-risk settlements. With core wind speeds of 125-135 kilometres per hour, it delivered more than 100 mm of rain over parts of Anakapalli, Visakhapatnam, Kalingapatnam, Kakinada and Machilipatnam, in Andhra Pradesh. But even though it has completed landfall, southern Odisha likely faces a greater threat only hence. Early reports claimed no loss of life in Andhra Pradesh or Odisha, which has been attributed to the disaster management operations in both States; the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister, N. Chandrababu Naidu, said there were five deaths in Andhra Pradesh . Regrettably, the suspension of transport services, including road connectivity and flights, closure of schools and offices, and power cuts to minimise risks posed by loose wires remains an essential part of saving lives, entailing other social and economic disruptions that the States must account for, and address, in their post-storm assessments.

Odisha may have to brace for rainfall and waters due to moisture in the storm’s outer circulation, which will arrive over land that has recovered in patches from the fourth wettest monsoon in the State’s history. Extreme rainfall after repeated flooding may face soil that has not drained fully, raising the risk of more flooding following even lower levels of rainfall, and slope failures in hilly terrain. Farmers in Ganjam and Puri have already voiced worries about the risk of prolonged inundation destroying paddy crops, compounding the already considerable financial consequences of the southwest monsoon; Ganjam alone had lost 33% of crops by October. In Sundargarh, however, farmers hope that Arnab will relieve moisture stress in standing crops after a dry month. The IMD has already issued alerts in the Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Kalahandi districts, before the rainbelt extends further north. The relatively low figure of deaths will be a testament to proactive governance. However, it is past time that States adopted a zero-disruption approach, especially since property and infrastructure were damaged, and the risk of people being pushed into poverty over lost possessions and livelihoods persists.

articles.title: Class 10 student attacked with wood-cutting machine inside classroom in A.P.’s Anantapur; accused yet to be identified
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The girl who was seriously injured in the attack is undergoing treatment in a hospital; two youths who allegedly carried out the attack were not students of the school, fellow students said
A Class 10 student of the Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu of Andhra Pradesh ’s Anantapur district was seriously injured after being attacked inside her classroom on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The accused allegedly attacked the girl with a wood-cutting machine after entering the classroom in the presence of a teacher while classes were under way, according to preliminary information. The victim was then shifted to a hospital for treatment.
The accused fled the school, leaving the wood-cutting machine behind in the classroom. The police said they are yet to identify the accused or establish the motive for the attack.
According to fellow students, two youths — who were not students of the school — allegedly entered the classroom and attacked the girl.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu expressed shock over the attack and enquired with officials about the girl’s condition and the treatment being provided to her. He directed the police to apprehend the accused at the earliest and take action against them in accordance with law.

“I am personally tracking her recovery and have directed the medical team to give her the highest priority care. I have ordered the police to hunt down the monster responsible and deliver the harshest legal punishment swiftly,” he wrote in a post on X.

I am deeply shaken and enraged by the barbaric attack on a Class 10 student inside her classroom at Raptadu ZP High School. Attackers who target our young girls inside schools have no place in our society. I am personally tracking her recovery and have directed the medical team to give her the highest priority care. I have ordered the police to hunt down the monster responsible and deliver the harshest legal punishment swiftly.

Nara Lokesh, State Minister for IT, Human Resource Development and Real Time Governance, also expressed shock over the attack on the girl. “I could not hold back tears in my eyes seeing my small sister lying in a pool of blood inside her classroom. We will crush the perpetrators with an iron hand,” he said, adding that any individual who think of harming a girl or a women is dealt with seriously.

BJP Andhra Pradesh State President PVN Madhav said utmost priority should be given to the safety of school children.

articles.title: Impeachment would have happened in Parliament if those in power had heeded public interest, says AISA’s Neha Bora | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: INDIA Bloc says everyone united in protests, 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today

Chhattisgarh Congress Legislature Party (CLP) leader Charandas Mahant, in a post on X (translated from Hindi), alleged that the BJP was snatching away fundamental rights and destroying democracy by “stealing votes”.

He said a “mega rally” would be held at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026, under the leadership of Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, and appealed to people to reach the venue and raise their voice to save democracy.

All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora said that if those in power had listened to public interest, the impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner would have been done in Parliament. She was speaking on the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today (October 31, 2026).

CPI leader D. Raja, arriving at Mr. Kharge’s residence for the ‘Public Impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar’, said “tomorrow’s rally will send a message to PM Modi that the country cannot be ruled in this way”.

Security was tightened outside the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Rajaji Marg in New Delhi on Saturday (October 31, 2026), ahead of the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ programme against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The symbolic exercise, modelled on parliamentary proceedings, is being organised by Opposition parties to highlight their allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged ‘vote chori’. It does not constitute a formal impeachment or removal process under the law.

JMM MP Mahua Maji said the INDIA bloc’s “public impeachment programme” was part of its push over the SIR of electoral rolls. She said civil society members and people whose names were deleted from the rolls were likely to attend, with an open invitation to MPs and leaders of other parties.

Congress MP Pawan Khera said the INDIA bloc’s exercise was “not a mock parliament” but “a public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. He added that people beyond the INDIA bloc, including members of civil society, were eager to join.
Preparation is in finishing touches for the Congress -INDIA Bloc Maharally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.

Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said a “major event” that “will be recorded in golden letters in history” was about to take place, with more than 10 lakh people expected to gather under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge.
He said the rally was aimed at protecting the Constitution, the country and citizens’ voting rights.

The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) on Saturday (October 31) questioned the timing of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally being held amid Diwali festivities and said that ignoring festivals, social harmony and the country’s economy in the name of politics is not a good sign for political parties.

articles.title: Woman rams multiple vehicles, tries to run over cops in Mumbai; booked
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The woman sped away after hitting a stationary car, knocking down a scooter, a motorcycle, and another car during her escape attempt, police official said

A woman allegedly rammed her car into multiple vehicles, tried to run over police officers, and created a ruckus at a traffic signal in the western suburbs of Mumbai, police said on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The incident occurred near the Sangeet Bharati Chowk signal in Juhu around 8.30 p.m. on Friday (October 30, 2026), when the woman sped away after hitting a stationary car, knocking down a scooter, a motorcycle, and another car during her escape attempt, an official said.
She allegedly also tried to steer her vehicle toward on-duty police personnel, he said.

"When a female police personnel tried to intervene and asked her to stop while recording the scene, the woman took out her mobile phone, started filming the officers, and created a ruckus," the official said.

A constable later instructed the woman to move her car to the side of the road to clear the traffic congestion. Several bystanders at the spot captured the entire episode on their mobile phones, police said.

Following a complaint lodged by the owner of the rear-ended vehicle, the Juhu police registered a case in connection with the accident and rash driving. Further investigation into the matter is underway, officials said.

articles.title: CPCB threatens to shut NCR industries yet to order pollution-control devices
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In an October 30 letter, the Central Pollution Control Board asked authorities in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to issue show-cause notices to non-compliant units under the CAQM’s revised emission norms

The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has directed pollution control authorities in Delhi-NCR to shut industrial units that have failed to place orders for installing or upgrading air pollution control devices (APCDs). Though not a new measure, it signals a tightening of enforcement of emission standards ahead of the winter pollution season.

In an October 30 letter, the CPCB has asked the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) and the State Pollution Control Boards of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to immediately issue show-cause notices to non-compliant units covered under the Commission for Air Quality Management’s (CAQM) revised emission norms. Units that fail to produce evidence of having placed orders for the equipment within five days are to face closure orders and remain shut until they demonstrate compliance with a credible installation timeline, the letter notes.

The direction comes ahead of restrictions scheduled to take effect in Delhi from November 1 under the government’s winter pollution management framework, which includes curbs on vehicles, construction activities and other pollution sources. After peaking in the “poor” category around 222–232 mid-week (October 28–29), continuous rainfall dropped Delhi’s average AQI to 60 on Friday (October 30, 2026) and around 95 on Saturday morning (October 31, 2026), according to the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology-maintained network.

The CAQM prescribed a particulate matter (PM) emission limit of 50 mg/Nm³ for 17 categories of highly polluting industries, as well as specified ‘medium’ and large ‘red-category’ industries, food-processing units, textile industries operating boilers and metal industries with furnaces. articles.title: Gujarat HC Judge strikes down ban on non-veg food sale in Somnath; two-Judge Bench stays her order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A division Bench stayed the judgment of Justice Nisha Thakore following an urgent appeal moved by the Gujarat Government, and directed that the Collector's notification banning the sale of non-veg food will continue for now

Hours after a single Judge of the Gujarat High Court struck down a ban on the sale of non-vegetarian food in the vicinity of the famous Somnath temple, a two-member High Court Bench stayed her ruling on Friday (October 30, 2026).

A division Bench of Chief Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak and Justice Nirzar Desai stayed the judgment of Justice Nisha Thakore following an urgent appeal moved by the Gujarat Government, and directed that the Collector's notification banning the sale of non-veg food will continue for now.
The division Bench will hear the matter next on December 26.
Earlier in the day, Justice Thakore allowed petitions filed by the owners of hotels and restaurants operating near the Somnath temple in Gir Somnath district and set aside the notification.
The Collector's order prohibits the sale of non-vegetarian food along designated pilgrimage routes.
The Government immediately filed an appeal before the Bench headed by Chief Justice Pathak, which stayed the single Judge's order late in the evening.

The notification dated August 10, 2026, restricting the "preparation, storage and sale" of non-vegetarian food within a 500-metre radius of the Somnath temple along with six specifically identified roads connecting important religious destinations in the area that form part of the sacred Somnath pilgrimage circuit would continue, the Bench said.
Hotel and restaurant owners contended in the petition that the restrictions infringed their fundamental right to carry on lawful business and earn their livelihood.

The State Government submitted that the constitutional freedom to carry on a business did not mean a person can conduct every form of commercial activity at every location, irrespective of the religious, historical and cultural significance of the place.
Somnath is not an ordinary commercial town but has extraordinary spiritual importance for millions of Hindus, the Government said.

articles.title: Congress is using democracy slogan to cover up electoral defeats: R. Ashok
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of Opposition in Karnataka Legislative Assembly R. Ashok accused the Congress of launching its campaign against CEC Gyanesh Kumar out of political desperation

Leader of Opposition in Karnataka Legislative Assembly R. Ashok accused the Congress of launching its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar out of political desperation and to divert public attention from its electoral defeats .

Addressing a press conference in Hubballi on October 31, he said the Congress questioned democratic institutions and the electoral process only when the results went against the party. The party had failed to accept the people’s verdict in several elections, including 59 Assembly constituencies in which it lost, he alleged.

“Why does the Congress have a different stand when it loses an election? It accepts the process when it wins, but questions it when defeated,” he said, referring to the party’s allegations of vote theft and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Mr. Ashok questioned the Congress’s claims about large-scale deletion of voters, including the alleged removal of 24 lakh names on account of death in Karnataka.

On the clean sweep by BJP in recent polls in Karnataka, Mr. Ashok said if the elections were held with EVMs, by this time Congress would have attributed to theft. “Through ballot, Congress has been handed a bullet,” he said.

The Congress is free to organise protests as part of its democratic rights, but threats to create unrest and indulge in violence could not be justified, he said. The campaign was aimed at reviving the Congress politically rather than protecting democracy, he alleged.
“The Congress should accept the people’s verdict and prove its strength through the ballot box,” he said, expressing confidence that the BJP would win 149 seats in the next Assembly election.

On the Karnataka government’s handling of drought relief, Mr. Ashok accused the Congress government of failing to provide the promised assistance to farmers. He said the BJP government, when in power, had released drought relief funds without waiting for assistance from the Centre .
He questioned the government of Karnataka over the delay in distributing the ₹2,500 assistance announced for drought-affected farmers and asked when the promised amount would reach beneficiaries.

He sought details of the funds received by Karnataka under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF). Rejecting allegations by Congress that the Centre had neglected Karnataka, he claimed that the State had received five times more assistance than before, even after accounting for devaluation of the rupee.

Referring to the ongoing protest by sugarcane growers , Mr. Ashok said the issue was serious and required a joint effort by the State and the Centre. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi had held discussions on the matter, and both governments should work together to address the concerns of farmers, he said.

articles.title: Deepavali sales expected to gain momentum in Coimbatore next week
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: With Deepavali falling in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to begin shopping after receiving their monthly salaries and festival bonuses; the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is likely to witness massive retail activity
Shopping for the Deepavali festival in Coimbatore city this year is expected to pick up next week across sectors.
President of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Coimbatore, C. Dorairaj, told The Hindu on Thursday (October 29) that several companies in Coimbatore will disburse bonuses next week.

With the festival coming in the first week of a month this year, people are likely to start purchases after getting the monthly salary and the festival bonus. So, the last 5-6 days preceding the festival is expected to see huge retail activity.
Be it textiles, FMCG, or household appliances, the retailers are expecting good sales this year.

All the products have seen a price hike, ranging between 10% and 30%, in the last few months, depending on the product. So, the retailers may see higher revenue though the volume of sales may remain the same as last year or slightly better in some sectors, he added.

In the case of textiles, while the large, multi brand retail outlets are already witnessing a pick up of sales, the smaller outlets are facing stiff competition from online sellers. Further, business at the small retail shops will go up in the last few days before the festival.

Though gold and silver prices saw a decline recently, jewellery retailers are yet to see business picking up. “We were hoping for better sales as the prices fell. But, consumers are waiting for further fall in prices,” said B. Sabarinath, president of the Coimbatore Jewellers Association.
The household appliances outlets are also expecting better sales only from next week.
In the case of sweets and savouries, most of the bulk buyers will purchase products for distribution just days before the festival, Mr. Dorairaj said.

articles.title: Coal India profit jumps 57% as higher offtake, prices weigh over costs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Cost of input materials increased 20% during the quarter.
Coal India’s net profit surged 57% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹6,547 crore in the second quarter, driven by higher offtake and improved price realisations that offset an increase in input costs.
The state-owned coal miner declared a second interim dividend of ₹10.25 per equity share.

Offtake during the quarter ended September increased 12% YoY to 186.34 million tonnes (MT), primarily driven by higher power demand. Average price realisation, covering fuel supply agreements, e-auctions, washed coal and other categories, rose 7% YoY to ₹2,346.21 per tonne.
The Kolkata-headquartered company’s overall production grew 4% YoY to 151.37 MT in the reported quarter, falling short of its target of 157.83 MT.
Revenue from the sale of products increased 21% YoY to ₹43,724 crore. Overall revenue also rose 21% to ₹44,179 crore.

The company’s cost of materials -- which primarily includes expenditure on explosives, oil and lubricants, heavy earth-moving machinery, spares and timber, among other items -- increased 20% YoY to ₹2,752 crore during the quarter.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds rates steady; pressure on emerging markets expected with stronger dollar outlook
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The U.S. Fed is expected to keep the rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market economies for foreign investors

The U.S. Federal Reserve held its benchmark interest rates unchanged between 3.75% and 4.0% at its October policy meeting. The 12-member committee had a 10:2 voting pattern for maintaining the status quo, while Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Federal President Beth Hammack voted in favour of a 25 basis points hike.
The Fed decision comes against the backdrop of sticky inflation, with the central bank awaiting more incoming economic data before changing the Fed Funds target range.

The Fed’s policy decision was broadly in line with market expectations, with Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh announcing the Fed would reduce the number of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings beginning 2027.

One of the FOMC meetings from next year onwards will exclusively address broader monetary policy strategy than rate-setting. In 2028, the Fed is expected to hold two meetings focused on monetary policy strategy, with the rest six meetings for policy, Mr. Warsh said.
While the policy decision was factored in by market participants, the absence of forward guidance by Mr. Warsh makes gauging the longevity of higher interest rate regime uncertain.
“I don’t believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis,” Mr. Warsh said. The market currently prices another rate hike by a quarter percentage point in December.

The U.S. Fed is expected to keep rates elevated, making U.S. Treasuries and the dollar relatively more attractive than emerging market (EM) economies for foreign investors. Combined with the escalating West Asia crisis, EM economies are expected to witness volatility and foreign fund outflow, economists noted.
On Thursday (October 29, 2026), the Indian market did not dramatically react to the Fed’s rate decision as it was mostly expected.

However, the Indian rupee declined to its lowest level in nearly 2 weeks on Thursday (October 29, 2026) following continued dollar demand. The rupee traded between 95.30-95.36 a dollar, down 8-14 paise from its previous close. While most other Asian currencies traded higher following the rate-decision, the Indian rupee continued to weaken.

However, economists are of the view that rupee is currently priced based on fundamental concerns and not on interest rates. This means the rupee’s depreciation is a direct result of risk-averse sentiment amongst investors amid the current escalating geopolitical situation.

The stock market too traded lower in early trade but trimmed losses, with the Sensex trading 852.58 points higher to 74,098.61 at 2.30 p.m. The Nifty 50 was trading above 22,900. Analysts note that the Nifty must trade below 22,500 for bearishness to pertain.

articles.title: U.S. Fed holds interest rates steady despite surging inflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The 12-member FOMC voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation

The US Federal Reserve on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) held interest rates steady, in line with market expectations, days ahead of crucial midterm elections where surging inflation has been a key issue.

The 12-member Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold rates at a target range between 3.75 and 4.00%, citing the need for more data in the fight against inflation, after having hiked for the first time in three years at its previous meeting in September.

“The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s two percent goal,” the Fed said in a statement announcing its decision.
Two members of the committee, Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, dissented, calling instead for an immediate 0.25-percentage-point rate hike.
The central bank has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

U.S. President Donald Trump's war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies. Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centres to support it. The decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party is seeking to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Mr. Trump's Republicans. Mr. Trump's handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.
U.S. consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7%, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.
Still, key policymakers at the Fed -- including Mr. Warsh -- have signalled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Mr. Warsh said that U.S. economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.
On Wednesday (October 28, 2026), the Fed said economic activity in the United States was expanding at a “strong” pace, upgrading its language from the FOMC meeting six weeks prior.

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP before the meeting that a decision to hold after raising rates in September was potentially contradictory, given the labour market -- the Fed’s other mandate -- has been largely stable.
“In terms of the economics of it, I don’t totally understand the logic,” she said.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure

S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

articles.title: How neoliberalism turned the world against its young
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The rise in youth unrest stems from failures of neoliberal capitalism, which has weakened public welfare and worsened unemployment; as falling wages undermine consumption and investment, young people face fewer jobs, rising education costs and an economic system that prioritises profits

France is in turmoil. And Albania. And Spain. Even India. As were Bangladesh or Sri Lanka earlier. The list goes on. While the specific demands may vary, one thing is common across these mobilisations: the young are on the streets. Why are the young angry the world over? In this piece, we look at the first world, in particular the G7 bloc, to understand why indeed.
France is a good example to understand what is happening in the global North. Emmanuel Macron, the antagonist according to the students in the French protests, has been in power since May 14, 2017.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia says intercepted ‘hostile drone’ in Riyadh region
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: No information yet on who launched the drone
Saudi air defences intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday (October 31, 2026), according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis.
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region," Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that "debris from the interception fell without causing injuries".

In recent weeks, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events — threatening the kingdom's economic diversification plans.
On Friday (October 30, 2026), Mr. Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam's second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim.

The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Riyadh.
More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since the fighting reignited, according to United Nations figures.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen's capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.
Later, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing Yemen's entire Red Sea coast in a lightning campaign.
The Houthis have reported frequent Saudi airstrikes in areas they control as Riyadh retaliates.

articles.title: Nations commit to get nature goals back on track at UN nature summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation

Nearly 200 nations struck hard-fought agreements on Friday (October 30, 2026) at a UN biodiversity summit, but the outcome was accompanied by disappointment over missed opportunities to address humanity’s destructive toll on nature.
Delegates cheered as crucial texts were approved in overtime but the celebrations were tempered by acrimonious debates and regret over limited progress on some of the most contentious issues.
The COP17 summit in Armenia sought to revive a landmark commitment to halt and reverse the destruction of nature by 2030 after global efforts to meet that goal fell short.
Over two bruising weeks in Yerevan, nations were urged to correct course to keep the pact alive and protect the plants, animals and ecosystems that sustain life on Earth.

The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation.

“And that’s it. Perfect,” said COP17 president Hambardzum Matevosyan in Armenia as he brought down the gavel on two major texts, the final versions of which were still not available early on Saturday (October 31).

But the outcome was “not commensurate” with the crisis engulfing the natural world, said French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut early on Saturday (October 31) as the summit drew to a close.

“The progress we failed to achieve here is a series of missed opportunities to speed up our response to the loss of biodiversity,” Ms. Barbut said in a lengthy statement sent to AFP , stressing that “nature will not wait for the pace of our negotiations.”
The final plenary stretched through Friday (October 30) night and well into the next morning, with negotiations turning sour as the hours dragged on.
Even as some delegates left to catch flights, others stayed behind to argue technical points.

Veteran COP observer Juliette Landry from the IDDRI think tank told AFP “there was a lot of push and pull in every direction” throughout the summit and “in that context, it’s hard to get things accepted”.
In a draft agreement of one closely watched text, nations were urged to “accelerate” their efforts and warned that “increased action” was needed to tackle the forces driving biodiversity loss.

articles.title: Trump backtracks on rallies in turbulent end to midterms campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The U.S. President reinstated two rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, saying Republicans “have a shot” in the midterms as a record 47.9 million Americans have already voted

U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday (October 30, 2026) insisted Republicans “have a shot” at success in the U.S. midterms , despite a feverish end to the campaign for elections that will decide control of Congress.
Mr. Trump reversed course and reinstated two rallies in Kansas and Iowa a day after cancelling them, a move that had raised questions about his health and about the state of the race.

“There’s such love in these all over the country,” he said of his rallies, before rattling off a series of insults against Democratic candidates vying for House and Senate seats in the elections on Tuesday (November 3, 2026).

Speaking late on Friday to a crowd in Daytona, Florida, Mr. Trump said the rallies were being held “for one very simple reason: to stop America-hating communists from taking over the United States Congress.”

He reiterated his promise to give every adult American citizen $5,000 if Republicans retain control of both chambers of Congress. Experts have questioned whether he has the legal authority to do that.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Trump acknowledged to reporters that a sitting President’s party often suffers in midterm elections. “I think we have a shot at doing well. Maybe very well, but you know, pretty well,” he said.

Republicans are defending their 53-47 majority in the Senate, while Democrats are seeking to capture at least one chamber of Congress and curb Mr. Trump’s legislative agenda during his final two years in office.

Mr. Trump has put himself at the centre of the Republicans’ midterm strategy, hoping it will fire up his MAGA (Make America Great Again) base. But his dismal approval ratings and public anger over the Iran war and the cost of living may be a drag on Republican chances.
Mr. Trump, who complained of losing his voice earlier this week, had lashed out on Thursday (October 29, 2026) when asked if he was scrapping the Kansas trip because he was “sick of traveling.”
“I feel perfect,” he snapped, saying he no longer needed to visit Kansas because Republican Senator Roger Marshall was “doing very well.”
But the about-face was likely the result of questions over the energy levels of America’s oldest-ever elected President, political strategist Mike Fahey told AFP .

“My suspicion is that Trump didn’t particularly like that narrative, and putting the events back on the calendar was the fastest way to kill it,” said Mr. Fahey, a veteran of multiple election campaigns. Both Kansas and Iowa voted comfortably for Mr. Trump in 2024, but have emerged as unexpected battlegrounds for Republicans.

fullParagraphs: Governor Kathy Hochul signed two laws on October 28 barring AI chatbots from harmful interactions with minors, including simulating romantic relationships and promoting self-harm, and requiring security safeguards in internet-connected baby monitors

articles.title: Oman rescues 25 from burning ship, Iran halts tankers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic
Oman said Friday (October 30, 2026) it had rescued 25 sailors from a merchant ship set ablaze in an attack, as Iran reported three oil tankers were halted while crossing the Strait of Hormuz.
Tehran has restricted maritime traffic through the strait since the West Asia war erupted on February 28 with U.S.-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic.
The narrow waterway, which normally carries about a fifth of global oil, has become a focal point of the conflict, with ships regularly coming under Iranian fire.

Muscat's navy "carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship RITI, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board," Oman's Maritime Security Centre said in a statement.
The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said, without giving details.
The Marine Traffic ship-tracking website described the RITI as a crude oil tanker.

U.S. Central Command chief Brad Cooper said in a video released on Friday (October 30) that U.S. forces had "successfully cleared the strait's internationally recognised primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines".
U.S. forces remain "present to ensure that all primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear," he added.

Mr. Cooper said he visited some of the more than 50,000 U.S. service members in the region, repeating earlier statements that Washington has helped Gulf countries export more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude via the strait since summer.

British maritime security agency UKMTO said that a ship 40 nautical miles (74 kilometres) south of Lavan Island in Iran was struck on Friday (October 30) by an unknown projectile, which caused a fire onboard.
"The crew of the vessel have been reported as safe and there is no reported environmental impact at this time," the UKMTO said on X.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said earlier that three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified "incidents" or hitting mines.

articles.title: Whose sight matters? How gender shapes access to eye care in India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Across their lifespans, from childhood to old age, women face disadvantages in access to eye health and care. For many, treatment depends on how their health is prioritised by the men in their household. Late care, or lack of access can leave girls and women with preventable visual impairment and loss

“I remember a patient, a little girl with retinoblastoma,” says Rohit Khanna, a community ophthalmologist and network director from L.V. Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad. “We told the family that the child required surgery and that the eyeball would have to be removed for her to survive. We were immediately met with resistance. The father asked, what was the point of her living if she was going to be disfigured. They would not be able to get her married later.”
Retinoblastoma is a rare, fast-growing tumour of the eye and is often seen in early childhood. It is a type of cancer, and can lead to death if not treated.

articles.title: AI giants promise publishers new way to block some
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every that crawls the web to collect data

OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic pledged on Friday to give media outlets and other websites a single way to prevent their content from being to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, amid growing criticisms and legal battles from news publishers.

Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every that crawls the web to collect data , but the new proposed solution will allow them to enter a single, standardized instruction that's recognized and honored by any AI company that adopts the protocol.
The solution will not fully take effect for months, though.

Microsoft will implement it beginning February 1, 2027, and Google sometime in 2027. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it will roll it out "in the coming months," while Claude-maker Anthropic said it has "already started" rolling it out.
The announcement comes as publishers are facing a surge in bots that scrape their articles to feed AI models. Some, like the New York Times, have taken the matter to court.

Meanwhile, internet infrastructure provider Cloudflare has blocked AI bots by default on new customer sites since July 2025, and a standard called Really Simple Licensing already allows publishers to charge bots that visit their pages.

The new setting will apply only to future training of models but does not prevent bots from crawling otherwise, and content will be allowed by default until the setting is changed by a publisher, Microsoft said in a blog post.
Opting out of AI training could reduce the chances that a publisher's content will surface in AI apps and experiences, Microsoft and Google said in separate blog posts.

"We believe creating a common signal that conveys such preferences to multiple providers at once is an important step. And we look forward to working with other AI companies on the standards and their implementation across the industry," Meta spokesperson Andy Stone wrote on X, conveying his support for the effort.

articles.title: How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: 12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues

The deaths of 12 infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, in Attappady in Keralam in recent months have once again cast a spotlight on a child health crisis that has defied solutions for over a decade. While the State government has set an expert assessment in motion, tribal organisations maintain that the roots of the crisis run deeper than healthcare, demanding sustained action on nutrition, maternal health, landlessness and the wider socio-economic conditions of the community.

Figures cited by tribal activists show that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011. Since 2012, Attappady has also recorded around 300 abortions, 90 intrauterine deaths and two dozen stillbirths. The region came under particular scrutiny in 2013, when 47 tribal infants died. Tribal observers estimate that around 10 children have died annually over the years.

articles.title: Launch of NVS-03: PM Modi congratulates scientists, engineers at ISRO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Mr. Modi also said that equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further India’s pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit the people

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) congratulated scientists and engineers at ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03 and said the mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, the country's indigenous satellite navigation system.
Mr. Modi also said that equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further India's pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit the people.

"Congratulations to our scientists and engineers at ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03. This mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, our indigenous satellite navigation system," he said in a post on X .
The Prime Minister said the dedication and ingenuity of India's space scientists continue to make the nation proud.

India's independent regional navigation satellite system NavIC was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on Friday (October 30, 2026) as ISRO successfully launched its navigation satellite NVS-03, which was placed into the designated injection orbit by a GSLV rocket.

The second-generation navigation satellite NVS-03, with indigenous and procured atomic clock, has a wide array of applications, including civilian use like real-time tracking of trains, vehicles and shipping vessels.

articles.title: Lava to increase smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Lava has been serving the sub-30k price category and is focused on budget and mid segment

As the rising memory shortages continue to hit smartphone makers, Lava has decided to revise its smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000. The homegrown smartphone brand said that the new prices will be effective November 15.
“In the current industry environment, ongoing memory shortages have necessitated a price revision of up to ₹3,000 across our smartphone portfolio, effective 15th November, 2026,” the company said.

Known to sell affordable smartphones in the country, Lava is the sole Indian smartphone brand in the country standing among Chinese and Korean players. During Q3 2026, the Indian brands, including Ai+, captured around 7% market share in India, as per Counterpoint.
Lava has been serving the sub-30k price category due to volume game and thinks that anything beyond that is vanity. It wants to focus on budget and mid segment and purely smartphone business.

Lava further added that consumers looking to upgrade their devices have a strong opportunity at this moment, as its products are currently available at festive prices across leading e-commerce platforms and offline retail network.
We would encourage customers to take advantage of the ongoing offers, before the revision comes into effect, added Lava.

Lava to increase smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000

Lava has been serving the sub-30k price category and is focused on budget and mid segment

As the rising memory shortages continue to hit smartphone makers, Lava has decided to revise its smartphone prices by up to ₹3,000. The homegrown smartphone brand said that the new prices will be effective November 15.

“In the current industry environment, ongoing memory shortages have necessitated a price revision of up to ₹3,000 across our smartphone portfolio, effective 15th November, 2026,” the company said.

Known to sell affordable smartphones in the country, Lava is the sole Indian smartphone brand in the country standing among Chinese and Korean players. During Q3 2026, the Indian brands, including Ai+, captured around 7% market share in India, as per Counterpoint.

Lava has been serving the sub-30k price category due to volume game and thinks that anything beyond that is vanity. It wants to focus on budget and mid segment and purely smartphone business.

Lava further added that consumers looking to upgrade their devices have a strong opportunity at this moment, as its products are currently available at festive prices across leading e-commerce platforms and offline retail network.

We would encourage customers to take advantage of the ongoing offers, before the revision comes into effect, added Lava.

articles.title: Small fish: On Operation Trident
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: While carriers of narcotics are caught in the net, big sharks operate freely

Operation Trident , a multi-agency crackdown on an international syndicate operating across the India-Myanmar-Bangladesh corridor, marks a significant step-up in the government’s campaign against drug trafficking. The Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eradicate drug networks across the country. The October 23 raids, which led to 18 people being arrested , were based on NCB investigations following the arrest of an alleged Myanmar-based kingpin in Delhi this May. However, the dismantling of the entire network would require identification of all suppliers in Myanmar and their successful prosecution. The government’s strategy, involving States and Union Territories, over 40 Ministries, central agencies and the pharmaceutical sector, is outlined in the Vision Document on Drug Control (2026-2029), launched by Mr. Shah at the Narco-Coordination Centre meeting on June 26, 2026. It envisages dismantling 100 major cartels and improving prosecution outcomes. The broad strategy reflects the complexity of the problem and signals a more focused approach. Data for 2025 also show an increase of over 50% in arrests and a nearly 53% rise in cases registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act compared with 2024.

However, the government’s action-plan will depend on consistent implementation and efficient coordination among agencies, and striking at the real brains behind it all. In several cases, foreign-based key operatives still remain at large and big sharks often do not fall in the net. The 2021 Mundra port case in Gujarat, involving the seizure of about 3,000 kg of heroin, is a case in point wherein the principal Afghanistan-based suppliers have yet to be brought to book. Also, the quantity of drugs seized does not, by itself, indicate whether drug availability or consumption has declined. Punjab remains a prominent example of the continuing public health challenges associated with drug abuse. The alleged drug-related killings of anti-drug activists in Mansa and Gurdaspur, along with the alleged death by suicide of a father in Sangrur who had raised concerns about the easy availability of synthetic drugs in his locality, underscore the human cost of the problem. These incidents also raise questions about the protection of those who speak out against drug trafficking and networks. These concerns lend urgency to the objective of dismantling entire networks and apprehending the “big sharks”, rather than concentrating disproportionately on individual carriers. The key is to identify the ultimate beneficiaries by meticulously following the money trail and ensuring their conviction.

articles.title: Fouled waters: On Rajasthan’s river pollution
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: River pollution from industrial effluents indicates state failure

The Supreme Court has pulled up, once again, the Rajasthan government over industrial effluents flowing into the Jojari river and the deadly risk it poses for the people depending on it. The problem is decades old — public interest litigation in the Rajasthan High Court alerted State machinery to the problem in 2011 — indicating an oversight by the State bordering on the systematic. The Jojari, the Luni, and the Bandi are seasonal rivers in the State’s arid western region, flowing through Jodhpur, Balotra, and Pali districts. This region has also evolved as a textile-dyeing and steelworking hub, and untreated or insufficiently treated effluents from these factories have run directly into the rivers and soil, endangering the health of around 20 lakh local residents. The region also suffers rampant illegal sand mining in riverbeds. The sewage treatment plants have been able to accommodate only around half of the sewage generated in the three urban centres, according to the State’s submissions to the Court in 2025, even as the Court recorded substantial underutilisation at common effluent treatment plants. The combination is suggestive of industrial sources bypassing treatment facilities, poor connections between the sources and the facilities, and/or insufficient capacity at particular sites or in specific periods.

The Court initiated a suo motu writ petition in 2025 and constituted a High-level Ecosystem Oversight Committee chaired by Justice Sangeet Lodha to audit the plants and draft a plan to restore the rivers. Based on the committee’s scathing status reports, Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta banned construction within 100 metres of the rivers’ edges and hazardous industries within 500 m of the present path, or of the flood lines where available. The Court has also upbraided local authorities for failing to enforce pollution norms by citing the Court’s own stay of a 2022 National Green Tribunal order imposing a compensation on the Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation and the local administration in Jodhpur and Barmer. The State regulatory apparatus has been dysfunctional: officials were aware of illegal mining operations in some areas, yet they regularised leases in those areas. Given the dereliction in play, the Court is correct to treat the possibility of collusion between State officials and industrial mafias seriously. Justice Mehta’s observation that the State could be held liable under the ‘polluter pays’ principle is also a significant indictment of state failure, through negligence. Now, importantly, the State still has to restore the Jojari and attend to its wellbeing, which is relevant to a recent tendency by the Court to substitute itself for regulators rather than disciplining them into discharging their functions. This needs to change.

articles.title: GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03 lifts off from Satish Dhawan Space Centre | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: NVS-03 satellite is equipped with an indigenous atomic clock alongside procured atomic clocks

The GSLV rocket carrying the next-gen navigation satellite NVS-03 lifts off from Sriharikota Spaceport. 18.46 minutes later, the GSLV-F18 is expected to place the NVS-03 satellite into the intended geosynchronous transfer orbit. Cryo-stage performance of GSLV rocket normal
ISRO’s live coverage of the GSLV-F18/NVS-03 mission will begin at 11:20 pm IST on October 30, ahead of the scheduled 11:51 pm launch from Sriharikota.

ISRO’s NVS satellite launch programme has seen considerable gaps between missions. NVS-01 was launched in May 2023, followed by NVS-02 in January 2025, a gap of 19 months. The next satellite, NVS-03, is scheduled for launch in October 2026, nearly 20 months after its predecessor.

The pace of launches has also been affected by setbacks in ISRO’s broader mission programme. The space agency recorded three failures in six missions launched from Indian soil between January 2025 and January 2026, adding to the challenges of maintaining a steady launch schedule.

Sriharikota [Andhra Pradesh], Oct 29 (ANI): A view of the NVS-03 satellite, which will enter the Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit in the 20th GSLV-F18 flight from Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), in Sriharikota on Thursday. The launch is scheduled for October 30. (@isro X/ANI Photo)

The United States operates the Global Positioning System (GPS), a satellite network that underpins a vast range of civilian, commercial and military activities across the world. While 24 satellites are considered sufficient to provide global coverage and optimal performance, the US maintains a larger constellation of at least 30 satellites. This additional capacity acts as a safety net, ensuring uninterrupted and reliable services even if some satellites malfunction or go out of service.

China, meanwhile, runs its own satellite-based navigation network, BeiDou, as an alternative to GPS and to meet its domestic and global positioning requirements. BeiDou’s global navigation services are designed around a constellation of 30 satellites, with estimates suggesting that approximately 35 satellites are currently in orbit.

Restoring NavIC to its minimum operational capacity would require ISRO to launch at least two more NVS-series satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, in addition to the existing NVS-01 and the upcoming NVS-03. These four satellites would form the minimum constellation needed to resume the system’s core navigation services. The launches would need to be carried out within a relatively short timeframe to ensure continuity.

However, four satellites would only meet the basic requirement. For greater reliability, stronger coverage and uninterrupted services, India would need additional backup satellites in orbit. This would mean building and maintaining a constellation of around six to seven NVS-series satellites to ensure the long-term stability of a regional navigation system like NavIC.

For NavIC’s core services to function effectively, at least four satellites are theoretically required. However, information shared by the Indian government indicates that only three of the constellation’s 11 satellites are currently capable of performing their primary functions.

These include first-generation satellites IRNSS-1B and IRNSS-1I, along with second-generation satellite NVS-01. IRNSS-1B has already exceeded its designed 10-year lifespan, making its continued operation uncertain, while IRNSS-1I could remain functional until around 2028. NVS-01, if it performs as intended, has at least another decade of service ahead. Meanwhile, NVS-02, launched in January 2025, was unable to raise its orbit after its onboard engines failed to fire, severely limiting its utility. As a result, NVS-01 is currently the only satellite that can be considered reliably operational over the long term.
ISRO’s NVS-03 launch could restore NavIC’s functionality, upgrading indigenous clocks and improving regional navigation amid recent launch setbacks.
