articles.title: Hungry customers won’t be able to distinguish between ‘Sangeetha’ and ‘Sangetha’: Madras High Court in trademark case
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice P.B. Balaji quotes Tamil poetess Avvaiyar’s statement, ‘Pasi Vandhal Pathum Paranthu Pogum’, and the Tamil idiom, ‘Pasi Kanna Kattuthu’

The Madras High Court has restrained a restaurant located opposite the Thanjavur Brihadeeswarar Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, from using the name ‘HOTEL SANGETHAS PURE VEG RESTAURANT’ after observing that hungry customers are likely to be deceived into believing that it belongs to the popular Sangeetha chain of restaurants spread across the world.

Justice P.B. Balaji quoted Tamil poetess Avvaiyar’s statement, ‘Pasi Vandhal Pathum Paranthu Pogum ’ (hunger could make one forget even the 10 virtues that he/she is supposed to follow), and the Tamil idiom, ‘Pasi Kanna Kattuthu’ (hunger could make your vision go blurry), to reject the argument that customers would be able to note the difference between ‘Sangeetha’ and ‘Sangetha.’

Passing interim orders in a trademark infringement suit filed by Sangeetha Caterers and Consultants LLP, the judge wrote: “A hungry person is the most potential customer for the respondent (Hotel Sangethas Pure Veg owned by Narayanan Chandrasekaran). He is not going to see or notice the colour scheme or the device marks used, but will easily get carried away by the name.”

The judge went on to state that though the respondent had dropped an ‘e’ from the name of his restaurant in English, he had still chosen to write the name as Sangeetha in Tamil. “It is not as if in Tamil language, there is no equivalent word or manner to replicate the English name Sangethas. It is very much possible to exactly convey the same spelling and even a different pronunciation, if really intended,” he added.

“In fact, applying the quote and the idiom that I have discussed above, a customer would easily be deceived by the name of the respondent and would be blind to the colour scheme, spelling, viz., omission of an ‘e’, use of ‘Hotel’ as a prefix or even the device marks (wheel and conch as against a veena used by the plaintiff) and is very likely to be carried away by the name and only associate it with the plaintiff,” the judge said.

Justice Balaji also rejected the argument that the plaintiff does not have any branches in Thanjavur and hence, there was no cause for confusion among customers. “Given the rich cultural heritage of this place, it is an undeniable fact that there is a huge floating population visiting this city, especially to see the Big temple... Given the number of visitors or travellers from various parts of the world to the city of Thanjavur, it is highly possible that they may only see the respondent’s hotel as that of the plaintiff’s,” he concluded.

articles.title: Theni jailbreak: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay orders suspension of Theni district jail superintendent in-charge
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: R. Krishnaraj, Superintendent of Madurai Central Prison, has been transferred and posted as Superintendent of Salem Central Prison

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has suspended Deputy Jail Superintendent N. Nageswaran, who had been holding additional charge as Superintendent of the Theni District Jail since August 6, 2024, in view of the jailbreak incident earlier this week.

A total of 17 inmates lodged at the Theni District Jail escaped from the prison on the night of October 26, 2026, after attacking the prison guard on duty. All of them were apprehended within a span of 40 hours.

Following the incident, Mr. Vijay on Saturday (October 31) ordered stringent action over the security lapses in prison administration, negligence in surveillance, and lack of diligence in the discharge of duties.

The officer was placed under suspension with effect from October 30, as per the Tamil Nadu Civil Services (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, for failing to pay adequate attention to the supervision and control of inmates and prison staff.

The Tamil Nadu government also transferred R. Krishnaraj, Superintendent of Madurai Central Prison, to Salem Central Prison to strengthen prison administration, accountability, and monitoring, a release stated.

The Chief Minister has also stated that Prison Department officials must discharge their responsibilities with utmost care and vigilance to ensure that there are no lapses in security and surveillance in prisons. He warned that stringent action would be taken against officials found to be negligent or careless while discharging their duties.

articles.title: PM Modi inaugurates tourism, infrastructure projects worth ₹307 crore in Gujarat's Ekta Nagar
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) inaugurated 23 development projects worth ₹307.83 crore to boost tourism and civic infrastructure at Ekta Nagar in Gujarat's Narmada district.
The Prime Minister also laid the foundation stones for eight development projects worth ₹118.88 crore, taking the total outlay for the 31 projects to ₹426.71 crore.
Earlier in the day, Mr. Modi paid floral tributes to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel at the Statue of Unity to mark his birth anniversary, which is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas.
The newly launched projects aim to upgrade visitor facilities and civic infrastructure around the world's tallest statue, which has developed into a major tourism hub.

The major tourism attractions inaugurated by the Prime Minister include an Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) hotel built at a cost of ₹50 crore, the Ekta Cruise (₹16 crore), a Rain Forest attraction (₹14.30 crore), and an Eco-Trail costing ₹3.67 crore.

On the infrastructure front, the Prime Minister inaugurated a sewage treatment plant built for ₹45.53 crore, a water treatment plant worth ₹21.40 crore, and a parade track and associated works costing ₹23.81 crore.

To improve connectivity and convenience, the government has introduced travelators worth ₹28.22 crore, a 24-metre colony road costing ₹23 crore to ease traffic congestion, staff quarters valued at ₹14.25 crore, and two nine-metre-long air-conditioned electric buses.

Other new facilities include a terminal building and a jetty near Mokhadi village, water stations at various locations, an extension of the walkway connecting Ekta Nagar railway station to the Visitor Centre, and fountains at different sites.
Mr. Modi also launched new visual features, including facade lighting within the Statue of Unity campus, the 'Ekta Prakash Parv' heritage display, and an upgraded Unity Glow Garden.

He laid the foundation stones for eight upcoming projects, including the Gora-Bhanadra Road estimated at ₹59.32 crore, and a Smart Zero Waste integrated solid waste management facility costing ₹36.58 crore.

Other upcoming initiatives include the development of the Khalwani Bridge (₹7.72 crore), a cactus and butterfly garden (₹ 5.79 crore), Khalwani Eco-Tourism development (₹5.15 crore), widening of Vaghadia Road, and construction of a disaster control room for the Sardar Sarovar Dam.

The projects form part of the Gujarat government's efforts to develop Ekta Nagar and the Statue of Unity area into a world-class tourist destination, with a focus on new attractions, improved connectivity and better civic amenities.

articles.title: West Bengal steps up efforts to bring back tigress that strayed into Assam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: West Bengal Forest Minister Manoj Oraon is all set to visit the tigress in Assam and finalise the plan to tranquilise it and bring back to Bengal’s territory
The West Bengal government is planning to bring back a tigress that was released in the Buxa Tiger Reserve and later strayed into Assam.

The three-year-old tigress, BTR-TF-1 (T-138), was released in Buxa on October 2 from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve as part of the State’s first tiger relocation project. However, the tigress crossed into Assam on Sunday (October 25, 2026) in search of a suitable habitat.
West Bengal Forest Minister Manoj Oraon said that he and officers of the department will visit Assam on Saturday (October 31, 2026) to inspect the tigress’s movement and health condition.

“Our team has already been coordinating with Assam’s Forest Department to monitor the tigress. However, I am personally visiting Raimona tomorrow and will finalise the necessary plan to tranquilise and bring her back to Buxa,” he said.

According to the officials, the tigress crossed the Sankosh River and a road in Gosaigaon in Assam to enter Raimona on Sunday (October 25, 2026), mostly in search of suitable habitat. So far, her movement area has been traced 25 km away from the Bengal border.

Forest officials from Assam and West Bengal, along with a team from the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA), initially decided to let her explore the surroundings and choose a suitable habitat. However, efforts are now underway to bring her back to Bengal’s territory.
Mr. Oraon said that the tigress is healthy and is also hunting animals.

On October 2, the tigress was translocated from Bihar’s Valmiki Tiger Reserve and released in the presence of Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Mr. Adhikari said three more tigers would be released in Buxa in the next two months, and the initiative would not only help in conservation of wildlife but also in boosting tourism in the region.

Buxa was declared a tiger reserve in 1983, and over the past few years there have been no reports of tiger presence in the region. According to an official statement by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the recovery of Buxa has been a sustained, science-based effort, and the Tiger Augmentation and Recovery Project, initiated by the Government of West Bengal with support from the NTCA and the Wildlife Institute of India (WII), has been implemented collaboratively since 2018.

Forest officials say this new tigress from Bihar will be subjected to intensive post-release monitoring using a combination of telemetry, camera trapping and field-based monitoring to assess her movement, adaptation, health and behaviour.

The protesters raised slogans against the government over price rise and the alleged deterioration in law and order. They carried sacks of rice, cans of cooking oil, and other essential commodities to highlight the increase in prices. They also held placards bearing slogans such as “Law and order has become a laughing stock” and “Wake up from your sleep, Chief Minister!”

Addressing the gathering, Ms. Kanimozhi referred to incidents of child abduction and alleged trafficking, accusing the government of failing to ensure children’s safety even within their homes. She also alleged that members of the ruling party were involved in “abducting and selling children.”

Questioning Chief Minister Vijay’s appeal to his supporters, whom he referred to as “ Nanbaas ” and “ Nanbees ” (friends), to persuade their families to vote for him during the election campaign, she accused him of seeking children’s support to mobilise votes without ensuring their safety.

Ms. Kanimozhi said reports of child trafficking had heightened parents’ fears about their children’s safety. She urged people to bring the government to an end, warning that Tamil Nadu risked being pushed into a dark period if the situation continued.

She also alleged that investments were not coming into the State, law and order had deteriorated, women were unsafe, and children faced an uncertain future. The administration had become so ineffective that questions arose about whether the government was functioning properly, she said.

The DMK leader also criticised the government over the rising cost of essential commodities, saying many families were struggling to afford even their daily meals. The increase in the prices of onions, tomatoes, rice, pulses, and cooking oil had made it difficult for ordinary households to prepare food, let alone celebrate Deepavali, she said.

She said rice and pulses had become twice as expensive. She also questioned the government’s claim that better-quality rice would be distributed through ration shops, alleging that the existing rice was merely being polished and presented differently.

Taking a swipe at Mr. Vijay’s references to gifts for children and women, she urged him to prioritise their safety instead of distributing presents.

“Please give every woman in Tamil Nadu a can of pepper spray,” she said, alleging that the police and government machinery were failing to protect women. She suggested that pepper spray be distributed through ration shops to help women defend themselves.
Former Ministers P.K. Sekarbabu and Poongothai Aladi Aruna, along with district-level functionaries, participated in the protest.

articles.title: Violence in Punganur: High Court hears Midhun Reddy’s plea to quash FIRs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Midhun Reddy's counsel argued that the cases were foisted on frivolous grounds

Justice Y. Lakshmana Rao of the Andhra Pradesh High Court heard the petitions filed by Rajampet MP P.V. Midhun Reddy for quashing four FIRs registered against him by Punganur urban police for alleged involvement in violence over filing of nominations for the local body election.
Appearing for Mr. Midhun Reddy, Senior Counsel O. Manohar Reddy argued that the cases were foisted on frivolous grounds for vexatious reasons.
Public Prosecutor M. Lakshminarayana appeared for the State. He presented videos to establish the involvement of the MP in the incident.

Senior Advocate Posani Venkateshwarlu appeared for one of the complainants and argued that the presence of the MP and his followers at the nomination centre was unwarranted and that he has no right to seek any relief when sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita invoked against him disclosed the commission of a cognizable offences.
Representing another complainant, advocate P.V.G. Umesh Chandra pointed out that the MP was neither a contestant nor a proposer and he disregarded caution by police.

He added that Mr. Midhun Reddy could not make out a prima facie case for granting stay, as there was evidence of a reasonable nexus. Moreover, Mr. Midhun Reddy's counsel submitted a medical report which revealed injuries to him. The matter was adjourned for a later date.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia says intercepted ‘hostile drone’ in Riyadh region
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: No information yet on who launched the drone
Saudi air defences intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday (October 31, 2026), according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis.
"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region," Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that "debris from the interception fell without causing injuries".

In recent weeks, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events — threatening the kingdom's economic diversification plans.
On Friday (October 30, 2026), Mr. Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam's second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim.

The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Riyadh.
More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since the fighting reignited, according to United Nations figures.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen's capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.
Later, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing Yemen's entire Red Sea coast in a lightning campaign.
The Houthis have reported frequent Saudi airstrikes in areas they control as Riyadh retaliates.

articles.title: Nations commit to get nature goals back on track at UN nature summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation

Nearly 200 nations struck hard-fought agreements on Friday (October 30, 2026) at a UN biodiversity summit, but the outcome was accompanied by disappointment over missed opportunities to address humanity’s destructive toll on nature.
Delegates cheered as crucial texts were approved in overtime but the celebrations were tempered by acrimonious debates and regret over limited progress on some of the most contentious issues.
The COP17 summit in Armenia sought to revive a landmark commitment to halt and reverse the destruction of nature by 2030 after global efforts to meet that goal fell short.
Over two bruising weeks in Yerevan, nations were urged to correct course to keep the pact alive and protect the plants, animals and ecosystems that sustain life on Earth.

The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30% of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation.

“And that’s it. Perfect,” said COP17 president Hambardzum Matevosyan in Armenia as he brought down the gavel on two major texts, the final versions of which were still not available early on Saturday (October 31).

But the outcome was “not commensurate” with the crisis engulfing the natural world, said French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut early on Saturday (October 31) as the summit drew to a close.

“The progress we failed to achieve here is a series of missed opportunities to speed up our response to the loss of biodiversity,” Ms. Barbut said in a lengthy statement sent to AFP , stressing that “nature will not wait for the pace of our negotiations.”
The final plenary stretched through Friday (October 30) night and well into the next morning, with negotiations turning sour as the hours dragged on.
Even as some delegates left to catch flights, others stayed behind to argue technical points.

Veteran COP observer Juliette Landry from the IDDRI think tank told AFP “there was a lot of push and pull in every direction” throughout the summit and “in that context, it’s hard to get things accepted”.
In a draft agreement of one closely watched text, nations were urged to “accelerate” their efforts and warned that “increased action” was needed to tackle the forces driving biodiversity loss.

articles.title: New York restricts AI chatbot interactions with children | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Governor Kathy Hochul signed two laws on October 28 barring AI chatbots from harmful interactions with minors, including simulating romantic relationships and promoting self-harm, and requiring security safeguards in internet-connected baby monitors

The story so far: “As a mother and grandmother, I believe kids deserve to be kids, without dangerous AI chatbots putting their safety and mental health at risk,...Big Tech, you’re on notice,” New York Governor Kathy Hochul wrote on social media after signing two bills on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) aimed at protecting children from the risks associated with artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots and internet-connected baby monitors.

The legislation prohibits AI chatbots from engaging in potentially harmful interactions with minors, including simulating romantic relationships, encouraging emotional dependency, and promoting self-harm. It also requires manufacturers of internet-connected baby monitors to introduce safeguards against unauthorised access to audio and video feeds.

articles.title: Launch of NVS-03: PM Modi congratulates scientists, engineers at ISRO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Mr. Modi also said that equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further India’s pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit the people

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (October 31, 2026) congratulated scientists and engineers at ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03 and said the mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, the country's indigenous satellite navigation system.
Mr. Modi also said that equipped with enhanced capabilities, NVS-03 will further India's pursuit of self-reliance in critical technologies and support navigation services that benefit the people.

"Congratulations to our scientists and engineers at ISRO on the successful launch of GSLV-F18 carrying NVS-03. This mission marks an important step in strengthening NavIC, our indigenous satellite navigation system," he said in a post on X .
The Prime Minister said the dedication and ingenuity of India's space scientists continue to make the nation proud.

India's independent regional navigation satellite system NavIC was restored to its minimum operational configuration of four satellites on Friday (October 30, 2026) as ISRO successfully launched its navigation satellite NVS-03, which was placed into the designated injection orbit by a GSLV rocket.

The second-generation navigation satellite NVS-03, with indigenous and procured atomic clock, has a wide array of applications, including civilian use like real-time tracking of trains, vehicles and shipping vessels.

articles.title: Class 10 student attacked with wood-cutting machine inside classroom in A.P.’s Anantapur; accused yet to be identified
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The girl who was seriously injured in the attack is undergoing treatment in a hospital; two youths who allegedly carried out the attack were not students of the school, fellow students said
A Class 10 student of the Zilla Parishad High School in Raptadu of Andhra Pradesh ’s Anantapur district was seriously injured after being attacked inside her classroom on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The accused allegedly attacked the girl with a wood-cutting machine after entering the classroom in the presence of a teacher while classes were under way, according to preliminary information. The victim was then shifted to a hospital for treatment.
The accused fled the school, leaving the wood-cutting machine behind in the classroom. The police said they are yet to identify the accused or establish the motive for the attack.
According to fellow students, two youths — who were not students of the school — allegedly entered the classroom and attacked the girl.

Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu expressed shock over the attack and enquired with officials about the girl’s condition and the treatment being provided to her. He directed the police to apprehend the accused at the earliest and take action against them in accordance with law.

“I am personally tracking her recovery and have directed the medical team to give her the highest priority care. I have ordered the police to hunt down the monster responsible and deliver the harshest legal punishment swiftly,” he wrote in a post on X.

I am deeply shaken and enraged by the barbaric attack on a Class 10 student inside her classroom at Raptadu ZP High School. Attackers who target our young girls inside schools have no place in our society. I am personally tracking her recovery and have directed the medical team to give her the highest priority care. I have ordered the police to hunt down the monster responsible and deliver the harshest legal punishment swiftly.

Nara Lokesh, State Minister for IT, Human Resource Development and Real Time Governance, also expressed shock over the attack on the girl. “I could not hold back tears in my eyes seeing my small sister lying in a pool of blood inside her classroom. We will crush the perpetrators with an iron hand,” he said, adding that any individual who think of harming a girl or a women is dealt with seriously.

చిన్నారి చెల్లిని క్లాస్ రూములో నెత్తుటి మడుగులో చూశాక కన్నీళ్లు ఆగడం లేదు. గుండె బరువెక్కింది. రాప్తాడులో ఉన్మాది ఘాతుకం తీవ్ర దిగ్భ్రాంతికి గురి చేసింది. ఉన్మాదులను ఉక్కు పాదంతో అణిచేస్తాం. ఆడపిల్లలు, మహిళల వైపు కన్నెత్తి చూడాలంటే భయపడేలా చేస్తాం. పిల్లల భద్రత పట్ల నిర్లక్ష్యం వహించేవారు ఎంతటి వారైనా చర్యలు తప్పవు.
BJP Andhra Pradesh State President PVN Madhav said utmost priority should be given to the safety of school children.

articles.title: Impeachment would have happened in Parliament if those in power had heeded public interest, says AISA’s Neha Bora | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: INDIA Bloc says everyone united in protests, 'public impeachment' of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today

Chhattisgarh Congress Legislature Party (CLP) leader Charandas Mahant, in a post on X (translated from Hindi), alleged that the BJP was snatching away fundamental rights and destroying democracy by “stealing votes”.

He said a “mega rally” would be held at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1, 2026, under the leadership of Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi, and appealed to people to reach the venue and raise their voice to save democracy.

All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora said that if those in power had listened to public interest, the impeachment of the Chief Election Commissioner would have been done in Parliament. She was speaking on the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ of CEC Gyanesh Kumar today (October 31, 2026).

CPI leader D. Raja, arriving at Mr. Kharge’s residence for the ‘Public Impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar’, said “tomorrow’s rally will send a message to PM Modi that the country cannot be ruled in this way”.

Security was tightened outside the residence of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Rajaji Marg in New Delhi on Saturday (October 31, 2026), ahead of the INDIA bloc’s ‘public impeachment’ programme against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

The symbolic exercise, modelled on parliamentary proceedings, is being organised by Opposition parties to highlight their allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and alleged ‘vote chori’. It does not constitute a formal impeachment or removal process under the law.

JMM MP Mahua Maji said the INDIA bloc’s “public impeachment programme” was part of its push over the SIR of electoral rolls. She said civil society members and people whose names were deleted from the rolls were likely to attend, with an open invitation to MPs and leaders of other parties.

Congress MP Pawan Khera said the INDIA bloc’s exercise was “not a mock parliament” but “a public impeachment” of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. He added that people beyond the INDIA bloc, including members of civil society, were eager to join.
Preparation is in finishing touches for the Congress -INDIA Bloc Maharally at Ramlila Maidan in New Delhi.

Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said a “major event” that “will be recorded in golden letters in history” was about to take place, with more than 10 lakh people expected to gather under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge.
He said the rally was aimed at protecting the Constitution, the country and citizens’ voting rights.

The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) on Saturday (October 31) questioned the timing of the INDIA bloc’s November 1 rally being held amid Diwali festivities and said that ignoring festivals, social harmony and the country’s economy in the name of politics is not a good sign for political parties.

articles.title: Woman rams multiple vehicles, tries to run over cops in Mumbai; booked
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The woman sped away after hitting a stationary car, knocking down a scooter, a motorcycle, and another car during her escape attempt, police official said

A woman allegedly rammed her car into multiple vehicles, tried to run over police officers, and created a ruckus at a traffic signal in the western suburbs of Mumbai, police said on Saturday (October 31, 2026).

The incident occurred near the Sangeet Bharati Chowk signal in Juhu around 8.30 p.m. on Friday (October 30, 2026), when the woman sped away after hitting a stationary car, knocking down a scooter, a motorcycle, and another car during her escape attempt, an official said.
She allegedly also tried to steer her vehicle toward on-duty police personnel, he said.

"When a female police personnel tried to intervene and asked her to stop while recording the scene, the woman took out her mobile phone, started filming the officers, and created a ruckus," the official said.

A constable later instructed the woman to move her car to the side of the road to clear the traffic congestion. Several bystanders at the spot captured the entire episode on their mobile phones, police said.

Following a complaint lodged by the owner of the rear-ended vehicle, the Juhu police registered a case in connection with the accident and rash driving. Further investigation into the matter is underway, officials said.

articles.title: CPCB threatens to shut NCR industries yet to order pollution-control devices
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In an October 30 letter, the Central Pollution Control Board asked authorities in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to issue show-cause notices to non-compliant units under the CAQM’s revised emission norms

The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) has directed pollution control authorities in Delhi-NCR to shut industrial units that have failed to place orders for installing or upgrading air pollution control devices (APCDs). Though not a new measure, it signals a tightening of enforcement of emission standards ahead of the winter pollution season.

In an October 30 letter, the CPCB has asked the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) and the State Pollution Control Boards of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Rajasthan to immediately issue show-cause notices to non-compliant units covered under the Commission for Air Quality Management’s (CAQM) revised emission norms. Units that fail to produce evidence of having placed orders for the equipment within five days are to face closure orders and remain shut until they demonstrate compliance with a credible installation timeline, the letter notes.

The direction comes ahead of restrictions scheduled to take effect in Delhi from November 1 under the government’s winter pollution management framework, which includes curbs on vehicles, construction activities and other pollution sources. After peaking in the “poor” category around 222–232 mid-week (October 28–29), continuous rainfall dropped Delhi’s average AQI to 60 on Friday (October 30, 2026) and around 95 on Saturday morning (October 31, 2026), according to the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology-maintained network.

The CAQM prescribed a particulate matter (PM) emission limit of 50 mg/Nm³ for 17 categories of highly polluting industries, as well as specified ‘medium’ and large ‘red-category’ industries, food-processing units, textile industries operating boilers and metal industries with furnaces. The revised standard became applicable from October 1.

The CPCB’s latest direction follows reports that several industrial units have not placed orders for new APCDs or for retrofitting existing equipment, and have also failed to obtain adequacy assessment reports or exemption certificates.

APCDs are filtration and emission-control systems fitted to industrial exhaust stacks to capture particulate matter before gases are released into the atmosphere. They include bag filters, which trap dust using fabric membranes; electrostatic precipitators, which use high-voltage electricity to collect charged particles; cyclone separators, which use centrifugal force to remove coarse particles; and scrubbers, which use liquids to capture dust and certain gases.

The CPCB’s previous attempts at imposing deadlines have only had limited effect. Only around 200 of 2,321 identified industrial units had complied with the installation or retrofitting requirement by July 31, according to reports. Industries had cited delays in equipment procurement, higher costs and shortages of agencies capable of assessing existing systems.
Until the latest tightening, several units operated under an earlier PM emission limit of 80 mg/Nm³, with 50 mg/Nm³ serving as an ‘advisory target’.

articles.title: Gujarat HC Judge strikes down ban on non-veg food sale in Somnath; two-Judge Bench stays her order
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A division Bench stayed the judgment of Justice Nisha Thakore following an urgent appeal moved by the Gujarat Government, and directed that the Collector's notification banning the sale of non-veg food will continue for now

Hours after a single Judge of the Gujarat High Court struck down a ban on the sale of non-vegetarian food in the vicinity of the famous Somnath temple, a two-member High Court Bench stayed her ruling on Friday (October 30, 2026).

A division Bench of Chief Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak and Justice Nirzar Desai stayed the judgment of Justice Nisha Thakore following an urgent appeal moved by the Gujarat Government, and directed that the Collector's notification banning the sale of non-veg food will continue for now.
The division Bench will hear the matter next on December 26.
Earlier in the day, Justice Thakore allowed petitions filed by the owners of hotels and restaurants operating near the Somnath temple in Gir Somnath district and set aside the notification.
The Collector's order prohibits the sale of non-vegetarian food along designated pilgrimage routes.
The Government immediately filed an appeal before the Bench headed by Chief Justice Pathak, which stayed the single Judge's order late in the evening.

The notification dated August 10, 2026, restricting the "preparation, storage and sale" of non-vegetarian food within a 500-metre radius of the Somnath temple along with six specifically identified roads connecting important religious destinations in the area that form part of the sacred Somnath pilgrimage circuit would continue, the Bench said.
Hotel and restaurant owners contended in the petition that the restrictions infringed their fundamental right to carry on lawful business and earn their livelihood.

The State Government submitted that the constitutional freedom to carry on a business did not mean a person can conduct every form of commercial activity at every location, irrespective of the religious, historical and cultural significance of the place.
Somnath is not an ordinary commercial town but has extraordinary spiritual importance for millions of Hindus, the Government said.

articles.title: Congress is using democracy slogan to cover up electoral defeats: R. Ashok
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of Opposition in Karnataka Legislative Assembly R. Ashok accused the Congress of launching its campaign against CEC Gyanesh Kumar out of political desperation

Leader of Opposition in Karnataka Legislative Assembly R. Ashok accused the Congress of launching its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar out of political desperation and to divert public attention from its electoral defeats .

Addressing a press conference in Hubballi on October 31, he said the Congress questioned democratic institutions and the electoral process only when the results went against the party. The party had failed to accept the people’s verdict in several elections, including 59 Assembly constituencies in which it lost, he alleged.

“Why does the Congress have a different stand when it loses an election? It accepts the process when it wins, but questions it when defeated,” he said, referring to the party’s allegations of vote theft and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Mr. Ashok questioned the Congress’s claims about large-scale deletion of voters, including the alleged removal of 24 lakh names on account of death in Karnataka.

On the clean sweep by BJP in recent polls in Karnataka, Mr. Ashok said if the elections were held with EVMs, by this time Congress would have attributed to theft. “Through ballot, Congress has been handed a bullet,” he said.

The Congress is free to organise protests as part of its democratic rights, but threats to create unrest and indulge in violence could not be justified, he said. The campaign was aimed at reviving the Congress politically rather than protecting democracy, he alleged.
“The Congress should accept the people’s verdict and prove its strength through the ballot box,” he said, expressing confidence that the BJP would win 149 seats in the next Assembly election.

On the Karnataka government’s handling of drought relief, Mr. Ashok accused the Congress government of failing to provide the promised assistance to farmers. He said the BJP government, when in power, had released drought relief funds without waiting for assistance from the Centre .
He questioned the government of Karnataka over the delay in distributing the ₹2,500 assistance announced for drought-affected farmers and asked when the promised amount would reach beneficiaries.

He sought details of the funds received by Karnataka under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF). Rejecting allegations by Congress that the Centre had neglected Karnataka, he claimed that the State had received five times more assistance than before, even after accounting for devaluation of the rupee.

Referring to the ongoing protest by sugarcane growers , Mr. Ashok said the issue was serious and required a joint effort by the State and the Centre. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi had held discussions on the matter, and both governments should work together to address the concerns of farmers, he said.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Across their lifespans, from childhood to old age, women face disadvantages in access to eye health and care. For many, treatment depends on how their health is prioritised by the men in their household. Late care, or lack of access can leave girls and women with preventable visual impairment and loss

“I remember a patient, a little girl with retinoblastoma,” says Rohit Khanna, a community ophthalmologist and network director from L.V. Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad. “We told the family that the child required surgery and that the eyeball would have to be removed for her to survive. We were immediately met with resistance. The father asked, what was the point of her living if she was going to be disfigured. They would not be able to get her married later.”
Retinoblastoma is a rare, fast-growing tumour of the eye and is often seen in early childhood. It is a type of cancer, and can lead to death if not treated.

Across their lifespans, from childhood to old age, women face disadvantages in access to eye health and care. articles.title: AI giants promise publishers new way to block some
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every that crawls the web to collect data

OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic pledged on Friday to give media outlets and other websites a single way to prevent their content from being to train artificial intelligence (AI) models, amid growing criticisms and legal battles from news publishers.

Publishers currently have to implement multiple blocking commands for every that crawls the web to collect data , but the new proposed solution will allow them to enter a single, standardized instruction that's recognized and honored by any AI company that adopts the protocol.
The solution will not fully take effect for months, though.

Microsoft will implement it beginning February 1, 2027, and Google sometime in 2027. ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said it will roll it out "in the coming months," while Claude-maker Anthropic said it has "already started" rolling it out.
The announcement comes as publishers are facing a surge in bots that scrape their articles to feed AI models. Some, like the New York Times, have taken the matter to court.

Meanwhile, internet infrastructure provider Cloudflare has blocked AI bots by default on new customer sites since July 2025, and a standard called Really Simple Licensing already allows publishers to charge bots that visit their pages.

The new setting will apply only to future training of models but does not prevent bots from crawling otherwise, and content will be allowed by default until the setting is changed by a publisher, Microsoft said in a blog post.
Opting out of AI training could reduce the chances that a publisher's content will surface in AI apps and experiences, Microsoft and Google said in separate blog posts.

"We believe creating a common signal that conveys such preferences to multiple providers at once is an important step. And we look forward to working with other AI companies on the standards and their implementation across the industry," Meta spokesperson Andy Stone wrote on X, conveying his support for the effort.

articles.title: How infant deaths in Keralam’s Attappady expose a deep-rooted health, social crisis
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: 12 infants, including 10 tribals, have died in Attappady this year, sparking a political row as the State government orders an expert probe. Tribal activists say the crisis demands action beyond healthcare, addressing malnutrition, anaemia and deep-rooted social issues

The deaths of 12 infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, in Attappady in Keralam in recent months have once again cast a spotlight on a child health crisis that has defied solutions for over a decade. While the State government has set an expert assessment in motion, tribal organisations maintain that the roots of the crisis run deeper than healthcare, demanding sustained action on nutrition, maternal health, landlessness and the wider socio-economic conditions of the community.

Figures cited by tribal activists show that 124 infants have died in the region since 2011. Since 2012, Attappady has also recorded around 300 abortions, 90 intrauterine deaths and two dozen stillbirths. The region came under particular scrutiny in 2013, when 47 tribal infants died. Tribal observers estimate that around 10 children have died annually over the years.

articles.title: Aavin to invest proceeds from sale of sweets in welfare of dairy farmers
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Aavin will plough back 90% of the proceeds from the sale of sweets this festive season to invest in the welfare of dairy farmers, official sources said. “We have not increased milk prices, despite the procurement prices having gone up. We are balancing the welfare of the farmers’ cooperatives and our loyal consumers with quality goods at affordable prices,” a source said.
People have been supporting Aavin for its quality. Many corporates have booked sweets and savouries in bulk for supply in the run up to Deepavali, the source added.

All of Aavin’s major outlets in the city and elsewhere are already stocking 250 gram packets of ghee badhusha (₹205), nuts halwa (₹200), kaju pista roll (₹340) and kaju katli (₹280). The sweets come in assorted packets too – 250 grams and 500 grams priced at ₹240 and ₹475 each. They also have savouries – 200 gram packets of butter murukku priced at ₹95 each and similar sized packets of special mixture priced at ₹110 each.

Like in the previous years, Aavin is producing sweets using its own ghee, butter, and khoa at its Ambattur dairy. “We are following FSSAI norms and are ensuring that sugar is added in the right proportions. Single use oil is used to fry the eatables. We do not use hydrogenated vegetable oil. Quality check is being done at all stages,” another source said.

articles.title: ED searches premises linked to Mudrex, Instadapp over alleged ₹4,600-crore FEMA violations
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Officials of the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) on Thursday conducted searches at three premises in Bengaluru and one in Madhya Pradesh in connection with an investigation into alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) involving unauthorised cross-border money transfers through cryptocurrencies, particularly stablecoins.

The searches were conducted by the ED’s Bengaluru Zonal Office on October 27 under Section 37 of FEMA. The investigation concerns entities associated with cryptocurrency platforms Mudrex and Instadapp, which allegedly facilitated cross-border financial transactions by using virtual digital assets (VDAs) to bypass authorised banking channels.

According to an ED press release issued on October 29, the investigation was initiated following complaints alleging large-scale FEMA violations by Bengaluru-based RPAS Technologies Private Limited, which operates the platforms Mudrex and Saber.money.

The agency said its preliminary findings revealed the alleged circumvention of FEMA regulations through an unauthorised cross-border payment system using crypto tokens, particularly USDT/USDC stablecoins. The entities allegedly advertised instant international money transfers through cryptocurrencies without the required authorisation from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
The platforms reportedly offered services to buy, sell, and swap cryptocurrencies, as well as convert fiat currency into crypto assets and back, facilitating international transfers.

The ED said its investigation had identified large-volume over-the-counter (OTC) deals involving shell entities, particularly those incorporated in Canada, Lithuania, the United States and other jurisdictions. These entities allegedly operated foreign-based cryptocurrency trading platforms to facilitate unauthorised cross-border transfers.

The agency also alleged that the entities used foreign-based cryptocurrency platforms to purchase or sell foreign-based crypto assets and settle transactions through Indian bank accounts, in violation of FEMA provisions. It further alleged that expenses in foreign countries were being paid using cryptocurrencies in contravention of the law.
The ED said its preliminary findings indicated that unauthorised cross-border transfers and crypto balances held on foreign platforms amounted to more than ₹4,600 crore. The investigation is ongoing.

Multiple teams of the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) conducted searches at the residence of former Minister K.N. articles.title: NIA takes over probe into alleged arson attack at Kadavumbhagam synagogue in Keralam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police cite suspected cryptocurrency payments, alleged reconnaissance videos and possible international terror links as grounds for a wider probe
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has taken over the investigation into the alleged arson attack on the premises of the 800-year-old Kadavumbhagam Synagogue in Ernakulam.
The move follows a directive issued by the Union Home Ministry.
Last week, the Kochi City police invoked the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against Ebin Paul, the accused in the case.

He was charged under Sections 15 and 18 of the Act, which deal with offences relating to a terrorist act and conspiracy, respectively. The provisions were invoked in view of the sensitive nature of the site allegedly targeted by the accused.

The police found that instructions had allegedly been passed on to the accused by other individuals. He is also suspected to have received certain payments in cryptocurrency. The police further claimed to have recovered videos showing him conducting reconnaissance of the location and rehearsing the crime.
The accused is suspected to have been involved in three arson incidents in Ernakulam district. Investigators had also found indications that he had identified targets outside the district.

Alleged communications recovered from the accused’s phone, containing references to sensitive targets, including Jewish places of worship, were among the reasons cited for a wider probe by the NIA. The police believed that the possibility of international terror links, the identities of individuals suspected of sending messages to the accused, and the financial transactions connected to the case warranted a thorough examination.

articles.title: Foreign Secretary to visit Kathmandu as plans get underway for Nepal PM’s India visit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nepal PM Balendra Shah is expected to visit Delhi by the end of the year, in what would be his first bilateral visit abroad, as he has been focused on domestic issues

In a visit to fine-tune the details of Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah ’s planned trip to India, Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri is expected to reach Kathmandu on November 4, along with newly designated Indian ambassador Sudhakar Dalela, a Nepali diplomatic source has told The Hindu .

Mr. Shah is expected to visit India by the end of the year, even as his seven-month-old government continues to deal with the aftermath of the devastating floods in the Bhote Koshi River while also planning a slew of administrative and political reforms.

If it materialises, this will be the first bilateral visit abroad by Mr. Shah, who rose to prominence during the September 2025 Gen-Z uprising in Nepal that overthrew the government of former Prime Minister K.P. Sharma Oli.

The Hindu had earlier reported that Mr. Shah, who belongs to the Rastriya Swatantra Party (RSP) led by former media personality Rabi Lamichhane, had vowed to focus on domestic priorities while deprioritising foreign interlocutors. In fact, Mr. Misri was earlier scheduled to travel to Kathmandu to meet Prime Minister Shah in May but the visit was postponed, ostensibly because of the new leader’s resolve to focus on domestic challenges.

Subsequently, RSP chairman Mr. Lamichhane was hosted in New Delhi and met Prime Minister Narendra Modi on June 3, after which Nepal’s Foreign Minister Sisir Khanal visited Delhi on June 5, in the first Minister-level representation to India from the new government, and met his Indian counterpart S. Jaishankar. This was followed by the visits of Nepal’s Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle in September and Home Minister Sudan Gurung, who participated in the first BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation) Home Ministers’ meeting held on October 13. Mr. Gurung also met Mr. Jaishankar before he returned to Kathmandu. Mr. Wagle paid a repeat visit to New Delhi to participate in a private media conclave on October 23, when he also had a courtesy meeting with the Prime Minister.

Despite the flurry of visits, the Embassy of Nepal here has been left without an Ambassador for some months since the previous Ambassador, Shankar Prasad Sharma, returned home. Diplomatic sources said that the appointment of a new Nepali Ambassador to India will feature in the talks with Mr. Misri.

Nepal now has a complex new process to appoint envoys, as the new government announced that top ambassadorial posts would be selected through a public application process. In all, around 4,400 candidates had applied for the vacant ambassadorial positions. Nepali diplomatic sources told The Hindu that Kathmandu is awaiting the agrément (diplomatic permission) from India for Nischal Nath Pandey’s arrival in the Nepali Embassy in Delhi. Of the top ambassadorial posts in 13 Nepali missions, three remain uncertain, while Mr. Pandey’s name, along with nine others, has received the necessary clearance in Kathmandu.

Mr. Misri’s upcoming visit is also expected to review Nepal’s requirements for dealing with the aftermath of the disaster in the Bhote Koshi River, which affected hundreds of Indian families as well, as many individuals remain missing.

The Foreign Secretary is likely to meet Mr. Lamichhane, who earlier this week paid a visit to Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand and the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati. The RSP chairman, who travelled to Uttarakhand by road from western Nepal, had described his visit to these pilgrimage centres as “personal and not political”.

“There are no political meetings planned. Since this is a personal visit, I urge people not to read politics into it,” he said, before starting his pilgrimage in his second visit to India in six months.

Mr. Misri’s conversations in Kathmandu may also include stakeholders from other political parties, though a final outlook on that is yet to be firmed up. It is understood that discussions may include a review of the Balendra Shah-led government, which came to power in March after the RSP’s sweeping electoral victory, defeating the Maoist parties and the Nepali Congress. Since coming to power, Mr. Shah has attempted several new initiatives, the latest of which includes an ordinance that will revise retirement age for government officials, bringing it down to 55 years from 58 years.

articles.title: Deemed ineligible: On the Supreme Court and SIR
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Supreme Court has pointed to the SIR’s flaws by design

At Wednesday’s hearing of a petition on the Delhi SIR in the Supreme Court, Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked questions that cut to the heart of the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s SIR of electoral rolls . If an existing voter was “lax, inert or did not respond” to enumeration forms, was that a ground for the ECI to “forfeit his or her right to vote forever”? The Bench headed by the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said that the ECI was in “error” to force such voters, struck off for not returning enumeration forms, to reapply on Form 6 as if they were new voters. It asked why voters who had shifted residences could not just disclose details and why deleted voters could not fill enumeration forms belatedly. This is the central design flaw of the SIR as it shifts the burden of enrolment from the state to the elector, including those who have voted before, and treats a mere change of address as ground for deletion. The share of draft deletions recorded as “shifted” or “absent” rose from 55% in Bihar to 72% in States/Union Territories in Phase 3. In Karnataka, about 84 lakh electors were deleted, marked as “shifted” or “absent” during enumeration. But only a net of 8.2 lakh, including new electors, were added during the claims phase, with the final roll being 64.5 lakh short of the projected adult population. Requiring moved voters to re-register as fresh applicants defeats the ECI’s historic mandate of widening the franchise, which was inherent in the 2002-03 intensive revision, where enumerators enrolled shifted voters at their new homes and the Chief Electoral Officer reconciled the old entries.

Justice Bagchi also mentioned that the Bihar judgment was not a “binding precedent” and that the legality of “logical discrepancy” checks, allowed only as an “interim arrangement” in West Bengal, had not been finally adjudicated. No statute or rule provides for judging a voter’s eligibility on the basis of family size or the age gap between voters and parents, which were two of the ECI’s ludicrous and algorithm-driven “logical discrepancy” checks. In West Bengal these checks resulted in massive disenfranchisement and The Hindu’s analysis found that in Delhi, Muslims were disproportionately flagged. But the Court should not merely issue managerial fixes such as extended deadlines or displaying printed lists in blocks, as it has in the past. The final SIR rolls are erroneous as deletions flowed from a flawed design rather than just lapses by the ECI. The dead and duplicate entries that the SIR identified should be removed and newly eligible electors added. Voters wrongly removed from draft rolls must be included again. The larger questions over the Commission’s SIR conduct and how its members are appointed must also be settled.

articles.title: Open to investigation: On the challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Public functionaries must not use privacy to seek exemption from scrutiny

The Digital News Publishers Association’s (DNPA) challenge to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 , and its Rules , has drawn attention to concerns that a law to safeguard informational privacy risks creating a serious chilling effect on the media. The absence of a specific exemption for journalistic activity could subject reporters investigating official misconduct or corruption to the obligations of a “data fiduciary”, requiring them to notify and seek consent from the very individuals they are investigating. Such onerous requirements could affect investigations undertaken in the public interest. The implications extend to routine newsgathering too, where personal information is integral to reporting. The omission is particularly consequential because the drafts in 2018, 2019 and 2021 carried a journalistic exemption. The Act already provides exemptions for certain forms of data processing, including for research and statistical purposes, making the denial of similar protection to journalists difficult to justify. Non-compliance can attract penalties of up to ₹250 crore, posing an existential threat to smaller and independent newsrooms. The DNPA petition also challenges Section 44(3), which amended the RTI Act, 2005, removing the earlier public-interest qualification concerning disclosure of personal information. The protection of personal information must not be absolute; an overriding public interest must remain a legitimate ground for disclosure, particularly when the information is held by public authorities. Investigations into corruption often rely on asset disclosures and tender documents containing personal data. Restricting access to these records risks reducing journalism to merely reproducing government releases.

The Supreme Court, while issuing notice on the petition, rightly emphasised the need to balance press freedom with the right to privacy. Although journalists in India enjoy no specific statutory protection for their work, freedom of the press is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a). The Court has also shielded newspapers from arbitrary state restrictions. However, growing mistrust of legacy media and the rise of independent content creators have made it difficult to determine who receives such protection. The Centre has also flagged this concern. Yet, carving out distinct categories is no easy task — a 2026 Reuters Institute report shows that the proportion of 18- to 24-year-olds identifying social media as their primary source of news rose from 21% in 2015 to 39% in 2025. A purely legalistic determination of these competing concerns may perhaps prove too onerous. Stakeholders must build consensus on a mutually acceptable framework where public functionaries and those handling public funds are not insulated from scrutiny under the guise of privacy. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s indication that he would meet editors is a welcome step towards consensus.

articles.title: Any plan to restrict sale of liquor in hotel bars and clubs located close to educational institutions? Madas High Court asks Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice N. Ramesh poses the question after expressing shock over a 19-year-old college student having consumed liquor at a bar attached to a hotel reportedly run by the college management

The Madras High Court has directed the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise to spell out whether any norms would be put in place for licensing bars inside hotels/clubs located near educational institutions in order to prevent incidents of underage students being offered liquor and ending up in fisticuffs in an inebriated mood.

Justice N. Ramesh issued the direction after expressing shock over a criminal case registered against a 19-year-old college student for having allegedly indulged in a brawl with fellow students when they were consuming liquor at a bar attached to an adjacent hotel reportedly run by the college management.

The judge suo motu impleaded the Commissioner of Prohibition and Excise as one of the respondents to an anticipatory bail petition filed by the college student and called for details regarding the licence issued to El Dorado bar at SRM Hotel in Potheri, near Chennai.

He also wanted the Commissioner to explain whether there were any rules, government orders, circulars or any other guidelines governing the grant and renewal of licence in Form F.L.3, and whether any of them prescribe a minimum distance from an educational institution, a students’ hostel or a place of worship.

The Commissioner was further directed to furnish to the court the distance between the bar and the nearest gate/ building/hostel of the educational institution measured along the path a pedestrian would ordinarily take, and whether the premises lies within a municipal area.

The officer was also ordered to state whether the proximity of the educational institution and the number of students studying there was taken into consideration before granting/renewing the FL3 licence to the bar in the hotel and what action would be taken in future.

Justice Ramesh also impleaded the SRM Institute of Science and Technology as another respondent to the petition and directed its Registrar to disclose whether the college management had any connection whatsoever with SRM Hotel and the steps taken by it to prevent students from consuming alcohol.

Taking note that three students who got injured due to a hit with a beer bottle on September 26, 2026 had been treated at SRM Hospital, the judge ordered that the petitioner should not be arrested until further orders provided he cooperates with the investigation and appears for inquiry whenever required.

articles.title: M.P. wildlife officials highlight Chambal region’s gun culture as probe into cheetah shooting goes on
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Speaking to The Hindu, an official said that the gun culture has emerged as a “crucial segment” in the probe and that the matter had been brought up with senior police officers

The wildlife officials in Madhya Pradesh have raised questions about the prevalent gun culture in the Chambal region even as they continue their investigation into the killing of a 19-month-old cheetah cub who was found with five gunshot injuries on October 25. The cub passed away on the morning of October 27 during treatment in Jabalpur.

Speaking to The Hindu , a high-ranking official said that the gun culture has emerged as a “crucial segment” in the probe and that the matter had been brought up with senior police officers in the region. The probe is yet to make a breakthrough.

“It’s a very complex dynamics there with almost everybody owning a gun so we will have to target this culture too going forward. There is need to review the criteria of issuing a gun license in the region and we hope there is some discussion about this at the government level,” the official said requesting anonymity, while calling for a crackdown on the illegal gun manufacturing in the region.
The conversation on gun culture coming up in the probe was confirmed by State’s Chief Wildlife Warden (CWLW) Sameeta Rajora.
Ms. Rajora said that all possible angles, including poaching, revenge killing or self-defence, were being explored in the probe.

On the evening of October 25, a cheetah monitoring team found the cub, which was wearing a radio collar for tracking, in a still position in compartment no. 748 of the Sheopur Territorial Forest Division on the border of Sheopur and Morena districts, about 50 kilometres from Kuno’s boundaries. During treatment in Jabalpur, five firearm metal pellets were recovered from his body, including one from his lung.

The two districts fall under the Chambal region, which was once infamous for its vast ravines and the dacoits hiding in them. Even though the dacoits are a fear of the past now, rivalries, high crime rates, and the tradition of owning a gun continue to thrive in the region. Morena is often in the news for its illegal arms manufacturing.
Officials from the region say a gun can be found in almost every household there.

The probe is being carried out by a State Government-formed special task force (STF) of forest and police officers, while a high-level team constituted by the Union Government also visited the area on October 28.
Sources in Kuno said that various teams had been mapping the area roamed by the cub for 15-20 days before he was shot for leads.

“Our teams have been mapping the area in which the cub roamed for 15-20 days before being shot and, more importantly, where he made the kills. We have also identified various illegal cattle camps in the area because it is believed that he was killed in revenge after he killed someone’s cattle,” an official said.

“So far we have not found any strong evidence indicating a poaching attempt, but it would be premature to conclusively say anything. We are making progress and should make a breakthrough very soon,” the official added.

articles.title: NHRC flags human rights concerns over parading of three persons in south Kolkata
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Commission took suo motu cognisance of the incident based on media reports and observed that the contents of the news report, if true, “raise serious issues of violation of human rights”

The National Human Rights Commission on Thursday (October 29, 2026) took suo motu cognisance of reports that three accused were paraded in semi-clad condition in the city’s Behala area and issued a notice to the Commissioner of Kolkata Police, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

A press release by the Commission stated that, according to media reports, three persons were found in a semi-clad condition with ropes tied around their waists in Kolkata. The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, “raise serious issues of violation of human rights”.

“A day before the incident, an 18-year-old youth and his 19-year-old friend, who were reportedly seen with a minor girl, were beaten and humiliated by the girl’s family members at her house. The youth’s father, whom the girl’s family summoned, was also assaulted. Subsequently, all three were stripped and forced to walk naked on the road at gunpoint,” the release stated. The Kolkata Police on October 27 paraded two men shirtless in their shorts with ropes tied around their waists. The two were held on Monday (October 26, 2026) for parading three naked men, including two teenagers, on the roads of a Kolkata neighbourhood. The police paraded the accused semi-clad on the same stretch on which the accused had forced the family members of the youths to parade a day before.

Civil rights organisations such as the Association for Protection of Democratic Rights (APDR) raised questions about the conduct of the police, saying that police were trying to “normalise revenge” and give punishment which the courts must be doing.

This was not the first time that police in West Bengal have paraded accused semi-clad as part of crime scene reconstruction. Several reports of accused persons being paraded not just with ropes tied to their waists but also in vests and underwear had surfaced earlier from Howrah, Kolkata and other parts of the State. The arrests, mostly of accused against whom several allegations of extortion have been made, have taken place after the Bharatiya Janata Party came to power in the State.

On June 5, 2026, the Calcutta High Court had observed that the State has the authority to arrest and prosecute individuals but cannot subject them to humiliation. “The police... can take action according to the law. If found guilty, they can also hang him. But they cannot deliberately defame the accused in the name of arrest,” the court had observed.

articles.title: Hike to help farmers, says CM; Ashok accuses govt. of placing burden on people
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar defended milk price hike by ₹8 on Thursday, saying that the decision was taken to support dairy farmers, Leader of Opposition R. Ashok accused the State government of placing an additional financial burden on the people.

After the Cabinet meeting that approved the hike, the Chief Minister said, “The hike has been made to prevent losses to farmers.” He pointed out that input costs, price of packaging of milk, transportation have all increased in the past one year. “There was a demand to increase the price by ₹12 to ₹15. We made this decision after consulting with everyone,” he said.
He also highlighted that all MLAs had demanded a milk price hike across party lines in both the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council, cutting across partylines.

Meanwhile, Mr. Ashok questioned whether increasing the cost of essential commodities and imposing additional taxes was the Congress government’s “guarantee to the people of Karnataka”. He said that while people were already struggling with rising prices, the government appeared focused on further burdening their pockets.

articles.title: 3,000 LED street lights to be installed in Vellore, Tiruvannamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With the onset of Northeast monsoon, Vellore and Tiruvannamalai Corporations will soon install an additional 3,000 new LED street lights in these towns to ensure the safety of residents, especially at night during monsoon.

Corporation officials said that a joint coordination meeting with key stakeholders, including Tangedco, the Revenue Department, police and residents’ welfare associations, was held at the civic body’s headquarters in these towns. In Vellore town, the meeting was chaired by Corporation Commissioner A. Catherine Saranya. “The meeting assumes significance as Tangedco was given adequate time before the start of heavy rains to address major complaints related to street lights,” K. Balasubramanian, Commissioner, Tiruvannamalai Corporation, told The Hindu.

Some of the major complaints reported by residents to civic officials were the snapping of electrical cables that are connected to street lights in these towns due to strong winds. Another complaint was the dangling of electrical wires on key stretches during monsoon. Corporation officials requested Tangedco officials in these towns to provide a separate electrical phase from transformers in each area to operate street lights alone. “Such an arrangement (separate electrical phase) will allow working of street lights even during unscheduled power cuts during rains. In other words, it will help residents to reach their houses safely,” a Corporation official said.

At present, 31,714 LED street lights and 124 high mast lamps are maintained by Vellore Corporation. In Tiruvannamalai, 13,700 street lights and 50 high mast lamps are run by the civic body. Of these, around 20 % of the total lights are run through solar power. On average, around ₹30 lakh is spent on electricity charges by each of these civic bodies every month.
Against this backdrop, the civic bodies have proposed installing at least 3,000 additional LED street lights. Most of these new street lights will be set up in extended areas of these two towns.

Areas like Alamelumangapuram, Rangapuram near the Collectorate Office, Ariyur and Sripuram will get new LED street lights in Vellore town. In Tiruvannamalai, all 18 villages on the 14 km Girivalam Path that are merged with the Corporation will get new street lights. “Better street lights will act as a deterrent against antisocials and stray dogs in the area. It will also help to prevent electrocution during rains,” said R. Padma, a resident.

Each street light, which will be 8 metres in height, will be installed at a distance of 30 metres from the next. High-powered 90-volt bulbs will be fixed on street lights at key stretches and arterial roads. The entire work will cost around ₹26 crore from the Road Safety Fund of the district administration.

articles.title: ‘Show me one Muslim minister at Centre, BJP-ruled States’: J&K Deputy CM
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: J&K witnessed a Cabinet expansion on October 27, with four new faces joining the Omar Abdullah Cabinet

As the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) launched a meme war at the ruling National Conference (NC) over recent Cabinet expansion and protests within the party, J&K Deputy Chief Minister Surinder Choudhary on Thursday (October 29, 2026) said the BJP, “which has no Muslim minister in the Centre or BJP-ruled States, has no right to criticise the NC”.

The BJP’s official handle on Instagram, with 338K followers, in J&K released a series of memes, showing J&K Chief Minister Omar Abdullah fighting own MLAs like Mubarak Gul and Abdul Majeed Bhat Larmi by editing the shots from gory Bobby Deol-starrer movie ‘Animal’. In another meme, the BJP edited characters from the comedy drama ‘Panchayat’ to show the heartburn the Cabinet expansion caused within the NC legislators, saying “endgame of the NC begins now”.

Countering the criticism and BJP spokesman Sunil Sethi’s description of “National Conference as Muslim Conference” over dropping a Hindu minister, Deputy CM Choudhary asked the BJP to identify one Muslim minister in the BJP Cabinet.

“Is there any Muslim who is a minister at the Centre or BJP-ruled States in the country. If it is about ‘Sab Ka Sath, Sab Ka Vikas’, why is there no Muslim minister in the BJP?. The party spokesman has no right point fingers at the NC,” said Mr. Choudhary.

The J&K Deputy CM also objected to BJP criticism over no Hindu representation in the Omar Abdullah cabinet. “I am a Jat from Rajouri’s Nowshera. Am I not a Hindu or Sanathani? Whatever I have become is because of Maa Vaishno and Maa Durga. The BJP needs to clarify if Jatts qualify to be Hindus or not. It should also tell us which ‘baradari’ are Hindus in J&K,” said Mr. Choudhary.

J&K witnessed a Cabinet expansion on October 27, with four new faces joining the Omar Abdullah cabinet. One Minister, Satish Sharma from Jammu, was dropped to accommodate more faces from the Kashmir Valley, where the party swept the 2024 Assembly elections and won 42 seats in the 90-member Assembly.

articles.title: A security deal, but not the end of the Arctic contest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The Greenland agreement strengthens American security while raising sovereignty concerns

The agreement signed between the United States, Denmark and Greenland on September 22, 2026, marks an important moment in the changing geopolitics of the Arctic. Greenland is an autonomous part of the Kingdom of Denmark. Under the 2009 Self-Government Act , it has extensive control over its domestic affairs, while foreign, defence and security policy remain with Denmark. Greenland came into the news this year because of the Trump administration’s repeated interest in gaining control over the island. What began as a territorial controversy gradually became a wider debate about sovereignty, security and the future of the Arctic.

The agreement, signed at the United Nations, expands the American military presence in Greenland while reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenland’s right to self-determination. It brings, at least for now, an end to the unusual tensions between Washington and Copenhagen over the future of the strategically important island. The agreement’s entry into force is subject to the completion of the necessary parliamentary procedures in Denmark and Greenland.
