articles.title: What does the shooting of a Kuno cheetah cub mean for Project Cheetah? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 19-month-old male cub, KNG22, died on Tuesday (October 27, 2026) after being shot outside Kuno National Park, the first such case since Project Cheetah began in 2022; the Centre and Madhya Pradesh have set up separate probes

The story so far: On the morning of Tuesday (October 27, 2026), a 19-month-old male cheetah cub died during treatment for five gunshot injuries at the Department of Veterinary Surgery and Radiology, Nanaji Deshmukh Veterinary Science University (NDVSU), in Madhya Pradesh’s Jabalpur.

The cub KNG22, an offspring of South African female cheetah Nirva, was brought to Jabalpur on Monday (October 26, 2026) night for an emergency surgery, a day after he was found injured and unconscious outside the boundaries of its home, the Kuno National Park (KNP) in Sheopur district. This marked the first instance of a cheetah being shot since the Union Government launched its ambitious Project Cheetah, a reintroduction programme in September 2022. The cub was cremated on Thursday (October 29, 2026) at the KNP.

fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Thursday presented trophies to Chennai, Chengalpattu, and Coimbatore districts, which secured the first, second, and third places respectively in the State-level Chief Minister’s Trophy 2026.

At a function held at Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Stadium in Chennai, Mr. Vijay also presented cash incentives totalling ₹6.85 crore to nine sportspersons, who won medals at the fifth Asian Para Games held in Japan.

According to an official release, Chennai district topped the Chief Minister’s Trophy with 142 gold, 97 silver, and 80 bronze medals. Chengalpattu district finished second with 64 gold, 43 silver, and 36 bronze medals, and Coimbatore third with 27 gold, 37 silver, and 54 bronze medals.
Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Thursday presenting cash incentives to sportspersons who won medals at the fifth Asian Para Games held in Japan. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
A total of ₹21.34 crore in prize money was distributed among 1,06,704 sportspersons who secured the first three places at the district- and zonal-level competitions.

Mr. Vijay also inaugurated the newly constructed Tamil Nadu Olympic Water Sports Academy at Pirappanvalasai in Ramanathapuram district at a cost of ₹42.90 crore, and a multi-purpose sports complex built at a cost of ₹20 crore on the premises of the Government College of Engineering in Salem.

He also launched the Sportspersons Development Assistance Scheme, which provides financial assistance to cover the personal expenses of sportspersons undergoing training at hostels and sports centres run by the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu (SDAT). A total of 2,600 sportspersons will benefit from the scheme, which involves an annual outlay of ₹1.77 crore.
Minister for Public Works and Sports Development Aadhav Arjuna, Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar, and officials from the SDAT were among those present at the function.

articles.title: Keralam CM V.D. Satheesan calls on Cheranalloor crash victim’s family, offers full support
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Satheesan says the government will always stand with them; family hands over a written complaint expressing their concerns to the Chief Minister

Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Friday (October 30, 2026) visited the family of Jayabalakrishnan who was killed in the Cheranalloor car crash and promised full governmental support to the kin of the victim.

articles.title: Namma Metro facilitates swift transport of human kidney for transplant
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: With Friday’s transfer, Namma Metro has facilitated seven organ transportation operations so far.

Namma Metro facilitated the swift transportation of a human kidney from Jalappa Hospital in Kolar to Fortis Hospital in Nagarabhavi, Bengaluru, completing the metro journey between Benniganahalli and Attiguppe stations in just 37 minutes on Friday (October 30).

According to a press release issued by Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL), the kidney was brought aboard a metro train at Benniganahalli station at 2.58 p.m. and reached Attiguppe station at 3.35 p.m., enabling its timely transfer for a medical procedure.

“Recognising the critical importance of time in organ transportation, BMRCL coordinated with the healthcare institutions and made the necessary arrangements to facilitate the journey,” release stated.

With Friday’s transfer, Namma Metro has facilitated seven organ transportation operations so far. These include one liver, four hearts and one pair of lungs, in addition to the latest kidney transfer.

articles.title: Nearly 1,500 police personnel for Sri Sathya Sai municipal polls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nearly 1,500 police personnel would be deployed across Sri Sathya Sai district to ensure peaceful conduct of municipal elections scheduled for November 1.

Superintendent of Police S. Satish Kumar told the media here on Friday that polling would be held in six municipalities, including Puttaparthi, Hindupur, Kadiri, Penukonda, Madakasira and Dharmavaram. “We have classified polling stations as normal, sensitive and hypersensitive and made security arrangements accordingly, with additional forces deployed in vulnerable areas,” the SP said.
Mr. Kumar said that civil police, armed reserve personnel, special parties and APSP forces would be pressed into service.

“As many as 61 striking forces, route mobile teams and special striking units would remain on alert to tackle any untoward incidents. CCTV cameras will provide continuous surveillance at polling stations and surrounding areas,” the SP maintained, adding that restrictions under BNSS Section 163 and Section 30 of the Police Act would be in force.
The SP appealed to voters to vote freely without fear. He urged people to report election violations to officials promptly and cooperate with the police to maintain peace.

articles.title: Candidates receive family support as campaigning draws to a close in Vizianagaram
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Family members of candidates from various parties played a visible role on the last day of campaigning for the Vizianagaram municipal corporation elections on Friday, with relatives, family members travelling from other cities, towns and villages to support the candidates.
Normally, close family members stay away from direct involvement in political campaigns. But this time their participation was noticeable in several wards.
Avanapu Vikram JSP-Vizianagram Parliamentary constituency coordinator along with others campaign in Ward 13 on Friday. | Photo Credit: ARRANGEMENT

As many as 50 families from different places travelled to Vizianagaram to campaign in Ward 13 for Jana Sena Party (JSP) candidate Kalla Rupa, who is the mother-in-law of Avanapu Vikram, JSP-Vizianagaram Parliamentary constituency coordinator. in . She is the mother-in-law of .

“Cyclone Arnab disrupted campaigning over the last three days. To cover all streets on the final day of the campaign, family members joined us and visited households in the ward. Their moral support helped to us take out a large rally,” Mr. Vikram told the media.

In Ward 22, Babametta, 75-year-old R. Lakshmi Bai and other family members campaigned for independent candidate Chitta Chandrasekhar Varma Raju. Ms. Lakshmi Bai, who completed her postgraduate five decades ago, said that all educated persons should enter politics directly. She said that she encouraged her son to contest the elections.
Businessman Attada Chandu campaigned door-to-door campaign for his relative independent candidate Attada Varalakshmi in Ward 30.

Former municipal chairperson Prasadula Kanaka Mahalaksmi along with other family members actively campaigned for Telugu Desam Party (TDP) district general secretary Prasadula Laxmiprasad’s wife Prasadula Rajani who is contesting in Ward 25 on a TDP ticket.
Kedarasetti Lakshman Murthy, a young businessman contesting from the 12th division, said that family’s complete support is needed for anyone to shine in politics.
YSRCP Mayor candidate Kolagatla Sravani said that her family members had played a vital role in campaigning all 62 divisions thrice in the last one week.
TDP mayoral candidate Avanapu Bharagavi’s family members travelled from Visakhapatnam and camped in Vizianagaram to support her campaign until the election process was completed.
Congress mayor candidate Ishwarya Lakshmi Yadav said that moral support from family members is essential for women seeking to establish themselves in politics..

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh SEC gears up for polls in 100 Urban Local Bodies on November 1
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: 36,351 police personnel, drones and CCTV cameras deployed to ensure peaceful polling; 400-plus flying squads to enforce Model Code of Conduct; counting of votes on November 3

The State Election Commission (SEC) is geared up to conduct elections to 100 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), comprising 13 Municipal Corporations and 87 Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats, on November 1. Polling was originally scheduled for October 28 but was deferred following directions from the Supreme Court after violent incidents prevented several candidates from filing their nominations. As part of seat adjustments, the Mayoral posts of the Greater Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada Municipal Corporations were allotted to the TDP and Jana Sena Party, respectively.

With the political negotiations and seat adjustments settled, the SEC has turned its focus to ensuring the smooth conduct of the elections. It has made elaborate security arrangements, deploying 36,351 police personnel under the supervision of 34 Superintendents of Police and 52 Additional Superintendents of Police. Drones will be deployed in sensitive and hypersensitive locations in view of the possibility of clashes between candidates and supporters of rival parties, which could lead to serious law and order problems.

CCTV cameras have also been installed at all polling centres as part of the surveillance measures. Elections to another 23 ULBs have been deferred owing to legal issues and administrative hurdles. Seventeen candidates have been declared unanimously elected as municipal chairpersons, including 15 from the TDP and one each from the Jana Sena Party and the BJP.
The SEC has appointed 28 IAS officers as general observers to oversee the election process and 30 IFS officers as expenditure observers, including two kept in reserve.

The Commission has also set up a control room at its office in Vijayawada to respond to any contingency. It can be contacted on 0866-2490023, 2490024, 2490025 and 2490026, or through the email IDs secyupsech\@gmail.com and seevapseed\@gmail.com.

As per the revised schedule, repolling, if required, will be held on November 2 and counting of votes on November 3. The postponement has also led to the rescheduling of polling for the Zilla Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) and Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) elections to November 5.

The SEC has laid emphasis on strict enforcement of the Model Code of Conduct, with more than 400 flying squads being deployed for the purpose. Security arrangements will also be strengthened at strong rooms where ballot materials will be kept after polling.

articles.title: Government plans balanced urban growth beyond Bengaluru, as demography shifts
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘The proportion of Karnataka’s population living in urban areas is expected to increase from the present 46% to 70% by 2047’
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday outlined a seven-point development agenda to drive regional urbanisation in Karnataka as he unveiled the Karnataka State Regional Urbanisation Plan, 2047.

articles.title: BJP-JD(S) accused of playing politics over Yathindra’s remarks about erstwhile royal family
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Backward Classes Forum president K.S. Shivaram has accused the BJP and JD(S) leader of playing politics over the remarks of Minister in-charge of Mysuru district Yathindra Siddaramaiah’s remarks regarding the erstwhile royal family of Mysuru.

In a statement here on Friday, Mr. Shivaram echoed Mr. Yathindra’s remarks about the inappropriateness of holding Jamboo Savari on the day of Rathothsava or chariot festival and emphasised that Mysuru Dasara must proceed according to the traditions practiced over the years.

With regard to the Mysuru Palace issue, Mr. Shivaram pointed out that the Minister, as a government representative, was only pointing out that the palace, which had been acquired under the Mysore Palace (Acquisition and Transfer) Act of 1998, was a public property.
As the erstwhile royal family had challenged the Act, the court’s verdict, whatever it may be, must be respected.

It would have been enough had Pramoda Devi Wadiyar of the erstwhile royal family of Mysuru clarified the matter and there was no need for BJP and JD(S) supporters to exaggerate the matter and blow it out of proportion.

He noted that no one can ever forget the contributions of Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar. His administration, commitment to social justice, equality, and development initiatives remain memorable to this day, including monumental actions such as granting entry to Dalits into the palace. Therefore, he urged the government to celebrate the next Dasara as the “Nalwadi Mysuru Dasara Naadahabba” and incorporate Nalwadi Krishnaraja Wadiyar’s name into the festival’s official title.

He said Mr. Yathindra had not spoken against the reign of the kings, but had merely referred to the legal framework of Mysuru palace as a government representative. “It is unfortunate that the BJP and JD(S) supporters are politicising the matter and resorting to personal attacks against the Minister,” he said.

Mr. Shivaram even pointed out that former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah had fought for social justice throughout his political career. “While everyone has the right to criticise him, one should maintain decorum in their language. Using personally derogatory remarks is unacceptable,” he said.

articles.title: Christa Pike says she feels constant pain in her first statement since failed Tennessee execution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital as the State tried to execute her on September 30 for the 1995 stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer
Christa Pike said she is in constant pain since surviving a lethal injection in Tennessee last month, but is thankful for the love and support she has received.

Pike issued her first public statement through her attorneys on Friday (October 30, 2026). She said she went into the execution chamber prepared to die in peace and woke up alone and confused in a hospital bed.

“There hasn't been a moment since that night when I haven't been in pain. My body hurts. My arms hurt. My hands hurt. My throat hurts. I still struggle to speak. And the pain isn't just physical. There is pain in my mind and in my soul,” Pike said.
Pike, 50, said she had not contemplated a life beyond her execution date.
"I'm deeply hurt by the incompetence that has put so many people in this terrible position. I continue to think about my victim's family and the terrible pain and loss they have endured,” Pike said.

Pike survived two doses of pentobarbital as the State tried to execute her on September 30 for the 1995 stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. She was 18 when she tortured and killed Slemmer with her boyfriend, becoming one of the youngest women to be sentenced to death.
She said she is thankful for the medical workers who saved her life and the people who showed her kindness.

“I don't know why I survived that night. I don't know what comes next. Some days, finding hope is harder than others. For now, I am trying to heal, one day at a time. And I am holding on to the love and kindness of so many people who have reminded me that I am not alone,” she said.

Pike's attorneys have urged Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee to reduce Pike's sentence to life imprisonment. Lee told reporters this week that, “I suspect her sentence will be the same as before unless determined otherwise by the courts.”
Mr. Lee called for an investigation into what happened during the failed execution and postponed the State's other lethal injection scheduled this year.
Friday's (October 30, 2026) statement was dictated to her legal team from the infirmary at the prison where she is housed.
Pike was hospitalised in the immediate aftermath of the failed execution and then moved back to prison at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Centre.

articles.title: 4,000 moved to safety in Bengal after Bhutan glacial lake outburst triggers flood alert
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: While the State government says the situation is currently normal, those living in the catchment areas of the Sankosh river and all its tributaries have been asked to evacuate
At least 4,000 people have been moved to safer areas as parts of the Darjeeling hills and the Dooars region in West Bengal were placed on high alert following a glacial lake outburst flood in Bhutan.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that the situation is currently “completely normal”. “Throughout the night, until 4 a.m., the SP, ministers, MLAs, and the DM were all on-site, working. They were also in constant touch with our control room here. The crisis is currently well below the danger level — it is in the ‘green’ zone. Furthermore, we have established contact with the people who were reported missing earlier this morning. All 47 of them are safe,” he said.

State Forest Minister Manoj Oraon said an alert for a possible rise in the water level of the Sankosh river was issued late on Thursday (October 29, 2026) night after the glacial lake outburst in Bhutan.

“After we received the alert, the district administrations in North Bengal took necessary measures. So far, over 4,000 people from 10 places in Kumargram and Tufanganj have been moved to a safe zone,” Mr. Oraon added.
He also said that, according to initial information received last night, some lock gates on the Sankosh have been damaged due to rising water pressure. However, the situation is stable now.

“We have noticed no further rise in water level in the afternoon. It is stable now. We are still communicating with the Bhutan government regularly and monitoring the situation. National and State Disaster Response Forces are also on alert ,” he added.

A glacier lake outburst flood (GLOF) which has originated from the Sintaphu lake at Mochu subbasin Gasa has been reported. The NCHM is currently monitoring the water level along the Mochu river at Tashithang. India has been informed. https://t.co/ArS7S73wd2
A graphic showing major rivers involved in glacial outburst flooding in Bhutan and adjoining districts on alert in India

In the morning, Minister for North Bengal Development Nisith Pramanik, who also holds the portfolio of Water Resources Investigation and Development, said a glacial outburst had occurred at Lemthang in Bhutan, with water from the lake flowing through the Mo river (also known as the Mofu river) towards the Sankosh.

In a video message, he urged everyone living in the catchment areas of the Sankosh river and all its tributaries to move to a safe distance immediately. Those living near riverbeds in Tufanganj and adjoining areas in Cooch Behar were also asked to evacuate immediately in view of the potential flooding. Loudspeaker announcements were made in riverbank settlements under the Rampur-I gram panchayat area, asking residents to leave their homes and move to designated shelters.

Nearly 7.4 million cubic metres of water had surged out of the breached Shintaphu Lake in Bhutan into the Mo river, raising fears of a sudden increase in the water level of the Sankosh, which flows along the West Bengal-Assam border.

VIDEO | West Bengal: State authorities have issued high-alert and evacuation warnings for residents living along the Sankosh River following a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) in neighboring Bhutan. State Forest and Environment Minister Manoj Kumar Oraon said, "Anyone who can is urged to immediately warn others in the affected areas. Special alerts are directed at the forest villages and hamlets bordering the Sankosh River, including the upper Sankosh forest village, the NKC Sankosh Tea Garden, Kumargram CD block, Chengmari, Valka Barabisa, Jharaguri and Pakriguri. If you reside along the banks of the Sankosh River in these vast stretches, please inform everyone around you as quickly as possible. A dam in Bhutan has breached. The floodwaters are expected to surge downstream within the next 1 to 1.5 hours. Please pass the word along without delay and evacuate people from these adjacent low-lying areas to safer ground, as the situation could turn critical. We must act quickly to prevent a disastrous situation like the one seen in Nepal." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd)

articles.title: Difficult negotiations lie ahead in Israel after Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The election results still need to be certified and submitted to the President next Wednesday (November 4, 2026)

Israel's final election results confirmed that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc lost its parliamentary majority and that weeks of difficult negotiations among very different parties, from ultra-Orthodox Jewish to secular to Arab-led, lie ahead.

The results released early Friday (October 30, 2026) showed Mr. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats in Tuesday's (October 27, 2026) election. The main Opposition bloc won 48. Arab-led parties secured the other 19, a historic showing. Now parties must meet, bargain and seek a way to team up for at least 61 seats in the 120-seat Knesset.
Mr. Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister, remains in charge.

“Now comes the truly hard part,” centrist politician Yair Lapid said on X, urging patience and adding, “If you want to know if something's happening behind the silence you're hearing now, the answer is yes.”

Difficult decisions lie ahead. Will the main Opposition parties that campaigned hard to unseat the divisive Mr. Netanyahu make the politically sensitive choice to partner with Arab-led ones? Or will they toss their vows aside to team up with Mr. Netanyahu in a potentially fractious unity government?

Friday (October 30, 2026) is when much of Israel starts winding down for Shabbat, and it was not clear who might be meeting with whom. Israelis debated possible coalitions and challenges, as some expressed traditional wariness around Arab parties and others insisted it was time for Israel to take a deep breath and embrace them.
“There are options for all of this, not like in the United States, where there are only two parties,” said Beny Engalrd, a resident of Tel Aviv.

The election results still need to be certified and submitted to the President next Wednesday (November 4, 2026). Then President Isaac Herzog will task someone with forming the new government. That could be the leader of the party that received the most votes — Mr. Netanyahu — or whoever the leaders of the various parties believe is best suited.
If multiple attempts to form a government fail, Israel faces a new election early next year. Mr. Herzog this week said he will do everything in his power to avoid that scenario.

In the hours before final results were announced, Mr. Netanyahu and his Likud party amplified unsubstantiated allegations that Arab-led parties had “stolen” the election, potentially with foreign assistance.

The Opposition quickly accused Mr. Netanyahu of demonising the Arab population, which makes up 20% of the population and showed up at the polls like never before in outrage over Mr. Netanyahu's far-right allies like National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. His party lost seats.
In Mr. Netanyahu's first public comment on Friday (October 30, 2026), he posted on X asserting it is forbidden to form a coalition with Arab parties.

articles.title: Israeli forces committed war crimes, genocide even after Gaza ceasefire: UN Commission
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: In Gaza, Israeli forces have continued expanding their territorial control, resulting in the killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians, including children, who approach or cross the Yellow Line, which separates Israel- military controlled Gaza from the Palestine-ruled parts of the enclave, Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar said.

Israeli authorities and forces have continued to commit war crimes , crimes against humanity and genocide in the occupied Palestinian territory even after the ceasefire agreement in Gaza, a United Nations commission of inquiry has said.

In a report presented to the UN General Assembly, the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory said Israeli military operations and settler violence in the West Bank were part of a coordinated attack against Palestinians, aimed at entrenching settlements, annexing Palestinian territory and displacing its population.

The Commission, Chaired by Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, said more than 75,000 Palestinians, including at least 21,500 children and 11,000 women, had been killed across the occupied Palestinian territory since October 7, 2023, the day Hamas carried out an attack in Israel, killing 1,200 people. It said the death toll had continued to rise despite the October 2025 ceasefire.

“Failure to act now is particularly egregious against the backdrop of the staggering death toll, which has continued to rise since the so-called ceasefire,” said Justice Muralidhar in his statement at the UN on October 26.

In Gaza, Israeli forces have continued expanding their territorial control, resulting in the killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians, including children, who approach or cross the Yellow Line, which separates Israel- military controlled Gaza from the Palestine-ruled parts of the enclave, he said.
The findings contradicted claims by the Board of Peace in its May report to the Security Council that the ceasefire had largely held and brought enormous relief to civilians.

The Justice said the situation in the West Bank had deteriorated significantly since October 2023. The commission concluded that Israel had committed crimes against humanity, including extermination, torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence. It also accused Israeli authorities of persecution through discriminatory rules of engagement that applied exclusively to Palestinians.

The report traced the roots of Israeli violence to policies dating back to the 1947-48 war, arguing that Israel had sought to maximise territorial control while minimising the Palestinian population through displacement and the use of lethal force.

The report also documents the expansion of Israeli military operations in the West Bank, including air strikes and the destruction of refugee camps. It says military operations since January 2025 have resulted in the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with 34,176 people still displaced as of August 2026.

Justice Muralidhar, addressing the gathering via a video link, also criticised Palestinian security forces for using unnecessary or disproportionate force against Palestinians in the West Bank. It said the Palestinian Authority had failed to conduct effective and impartial investigations into killings and provide remedies to victims.

Calling on Israel to end its occupation and comply with the International Court of Justice’s July 2024 advisory opinion, Justice Muralidhar urged Member States to stop providing assistance that could sustain the occupation and settlements. He also called on States to use all available means to prevent and punish genocide and support the International Criminal Court.
He said he was addressing the committee through a video statement because he had not received a U.S. visa despite efforts to meet the requirements.

articles.title: Saudi Aramco, Sonatrach raise LPG official selling prices for November, say sources
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Saudi Aramco's OSPs are used ​as a reference ‌for contracts to supply LPG from the West Asia to the Asia-Pacific region

Saudi Arabia's state oil producer Saudi Aramco ​has raised official selling ‌prices for liquefied petroleum gas by ​between 5.9% and ⁠6.8% for November due to seasonally higher demand and limited ‌LPG supply on global markets, traders said on ‌Friday (October 30, 2026).
Algeria's Sonatrach lifted LPG ‌prices ⁠for November by between ⁠23% and 40%, the traders said.

Saudi Aramco's OSPs are used ​as a reference ‌for contracts to supply LPG from the West Asia to the Asia-Pacific region ‌while Sonatrach's OSPs are used ​as benchmarks for the Mediterranean and Black Sea ⁠region, including Turkey.
Saudi Aramco's November OSPs increased by $40 ‌a metric ton to $720 a ton for propane and by $50 a ton to $780 a ton for butane.
Propane and butane are types ‌of LPG with different boiling points. ​LPG is mainly used as fuel for ⁠cars, heating, and as a feedstock ⁠for other petrochemicals.
Sonatrach increased its November propane ‌OSP by $155 a ton to $825 and for butane ​by $300 a ton to $1,050.

articles.title: ISRO set to launch GSLV-F18 carrying navigation satellite NVS-03 | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Restoring NavIC to its minimum operational capacity would require ISRO to launch at least two more NVS-series satellites, NVS-04 and NVS-05, in addition to the existing NVS-01 and the upcoming NVS-03. These four satellites would form the minimum constellation needed to resume the system’s core navigation services. The launches would need to be carried out within a relatively short timeframe to ensure continuity.

However, four satellites would only meet the basic requirement. For greater reliability, stronger coverage and uninterrupted services, India would need additional backup satellites in orbit. This would mean building and maintaining a constellation of around six to seven NVS-series satellites to ensure the long-term stability of a regional navigation system like NavIC.

For NavIC’s core services to function effectively, at least four satellites are theoretically required. However, information shared by the Indian government indicates that only three of the constellation’s 11 satellites are currently capable of performing their primary functions.

These include first-generation satellites IRNSS-1B and IRNSS-1I, along with second-generation satellite NVS-01. IRNSS-1B has already exceeded its designed 10-year lifespan, making its continued operation uncertain, while IRNSS-1I could remain functional until around 2028. NVS-01, if it performs as intended, has at least another decade of service ahead. Meanwhile, NVS-02, launched in January 2025, was unable to raise its orbit after its onboard engines failed to fire, severely limiting its utility. As a result, NVS-01 is currently the only satellite that can be considered reliably operational over the long term.
ISRO’s NVS-03 launch could restore NavIC’s functionality, upgrading indigenous clocks and improving regional navigation amid recent launch setbacks.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Tamil Nadu-head quartered Milky Mist Dairy Food, which listed on the stocks markets in August this year, registered 308.4% growth in profit after tax during April-September compared with the corresponding period last fiscal.

According to K. articles.title: Crypto platform Binance freezes $3 billion worth of funds after “security issue”
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: According to crypto security firm TRM Labs, attackers siphoned off approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on September 30.

The international cryptocurrency platform has temporarily frozen all deposits and withdrawals following a likely hack, the biggest on record so far, which crypto security firms are saying could have originated in North Korea.

“Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating,” Binance posted on social media early morning India time on September 30. “User funds are completely safe.”

“ Binance will cover all losses. As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement,” the company said in a subsequent post.
The company further said that the current verified total amount of funds that have been frozen is $3 billion.
“This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” it added.
The impact of the announcements on the price of Bitcoin was immediate, with the cryptocurrency falling 6% to trade at around $76,500 by Friday morning.

According to crypto security firm TRM Labs, attackers siphoned off approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, with most of the money stolen in about 20 minutes starting at 1.35 AM Indian Standard Time (IST).
“That makes this the largest crypto theft on record, about four times the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025,” TRM Labs said in a post on the attack.
The security firm attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, a major hacking network operating out of North Korea.
“We base this assessment on robust on and off-chain intelligence sources,” TRM Labs said. “The FBI named the same group as responsible for the USD 1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025.”

“Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack and the KelpDAO hack in April 2026: small Tornado Cash withdrawals funding an operator wallet, staging that began well before the theft, and signatures obtained in advance then executed in one burst,” it added.
It did, however, say that the pattern of laundering the stolen cryptocurrencies differs in this case from how it was done following the Bybit hack.

articles.title: TRAI proposes board-approved AI policies, mandatory reporting of serious incidents by telcos
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: TRAI said it has floated the draft ‘Guidelines on Responsible Use of AI in Telecommunication Networks and Provision of Telecommunication Services’ for stakeholders' comments.

Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), on Friday (October 30, 2026), proposed a comprehensive draft framework for the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in telecom networks that would require service providers to adopt board-approved AI policies, establish dedicated governance and safety committees, and report serious AI-related incidents to the regulator.

The draft guidelines, released for stakeholder consultations, also seek to make entities accountable for the outcomes of AI systems deployed in their networks and services, "irrespective of whether AI systems are developed internally, procured/ outsourced from a third party or a combination thereof."

A look at the consultation paper shows that under the proposed framework, telecom operators and other authorised entities using AI will have to classify their AI systems into high-, medium- and low-risk categories based on their significance to network operations, financial and operational outcomes, and potential implications for consumers.

Each entity will be required to formulate an internal AI policy, approved by its board of directors or equivalent governing body, covering risk classification, deployment approvals, incident management, human oversight, data governance and consumer grievance redressal.
"All AI systems shall be subject to an appropriate human oversight for risk mitigation as per a predefined mechanism," the consultation paper said.

The regulator has proposed that AI-related incidents be classified into four categories, namely critical, high, moderate and low severity, with critical and high-severity incidents mandatorily reported to TRAI.
"Critical severity AI incidents and high severity AI incidents shall be informed to TRAI in a prescribed format, manner and timeframe," it said.
Telecom companies will also have to maintain central databases of AI incidents and consumer complaints involving AI-related harm, with mechanisms for investigation, mitigation and resolution.
The sector regulator noted that, at present, AI is increasingly being integrated into telecommunication networks and provision of telecommunication services.

"With a view to ensuring consistent and responsible implementation of the India AI Governance Guidelines in the telecommunication sector, and to increase clarity, predictability and accountability in the ecosystem, TRAI has decided to frame guidelines on responsible use of AI in telecommunication networks and provision of telecommunication services after following stakeholders' consultation," TRAI said.

articles.title: Google parent Alphabet’s shares plunge 12.6% as investors question returns from AI spending
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Company reports 25% revenue growth, but quarterly infrastructure spending crosses $51 billion; lower advertising revenue from AI-powered Search queries adds to concerns

Shares of Google parent Alphabet fell 12.64% on the Nasdaq on Thursday (October 29, 2026), closing at $283.82. The decline wiped out about $482 billion in the company’s market value, marking its worst one-day fall since it began trading in 2004, according to reports.
Alphabet shares remained under pressure in Friday’s (October 30, 2026) pre-market trading, slipping a further 0.42% to $282.64, according to Yahoo Finance.
The sell-off came after the company reported its quarterly results, renewing concerns about whether its heavy investments in artificial intelligence (AI) will generate enough returns.

Alphabet’s revenue grew 25% year-on-year to $127.6 billion in the quarter ended September 30. Its net profit fell to $26.5 billion from $35 billion a year earlier, largely due to losses on its equity investments. However, earnings from its business operations rose 30% to $40.6 billion.

Google Cloud was a bright spot. Its revenue more than doubled to $30.7 billion, up 103% from a year earlier. The division’s operating income rose to $11.1 billion from $3.6 billion. Alphabet attributed the growth to demand for AI infrastructure and solutions, as well as its core cloud services.

But the investment needed to support this growth is putting pressure on the company’s cash flow. Alphabet spent $51.4 billion on capital expenditure in the September quarter, mainly on data centres, servers and networking equipment. The company said most of this spending went towards technical infrastructure to support its AI investments.

Alphabet generated $42.3 billion in cash from its business operations during the quarter. Since its capital expenditure was higher than the cash generated, it reported negative free cash flow of $9.1 billion.

Chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi said infrastructure spending was a major reason for the negative free cash flow. She also pointed to inventory being built up for sales of Google’s own AI chips, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs), and a $5.2-billion payment relating to a European Commission fine.

Alphabet retained its capital expenditure guidance of $195 billion to $205 billion for 2026. The $51.4 billion spent in the September quarter was roughly a quarter of its projected full-year expenditure. Ms. Ashkenazi said capital expenditure would increase significantly in 2027, indicating that the high spending is likely to continue.

Investors are also watching how AI is changing Google’s main Search advertising business. Revenue from Google Search and related advertising grew 12% to $63.35 billion in the quarter, slower than the 17% growth in the previous quarter. This is part of Google’s total advertising revenue of $82 billion, which also includes advertisements on YouTube and the Google Network.

During the October 28 earnings call, Philipp Schindler, Google’s senior vice-president and chief business officer, said the growing number of queries through AI Mode, the company’s AI-powered search service, was affecting advertising revenue. Google earns less from these queries than it does from traditional Search.

Mr. Schindler said Google was experimenting with advertisements in AI-powered Search features, including AI Overviews and AI Mode. He also said foreign exchange movements were the single biggest factor behind the slowdown in Search revenue growth compared with the previous quarter. Advertising trends in the retail and media and entertainment sectors also played a role.

articles.title: Over 2,200 police drafted for Tirupati election duty across five urban bodies
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The police department has drafted 2,202 policemen for election duty in the five urban local bodies in Tirupati district, which are going to polls on Sunday.
A lion’s share of the deployment goes towards the Tirupati Municipal Corporation, while the remaining is apportioned to Puttur, Naidupeta, Sullurpeta and Venkatagiri municipal towns.
The figure includes an Additional Superintendent of Police, eight Deputy Superintendents, 26 Circle Inspectors and 98 Sub-Inspectors.

“A Rapid Response Team will be in the waiting to tackle emergency situations in violence-prone and sensitive polling stations”, said the Superintendent of Police L. Subbarayudu, who appealed to the public to cast their vote without any fear.
Those trying to thwart the election process or disrupt peace in the demarcated areas around the polling stations would face legal action, he warned.

articles.title: Bursting of firecrackers only between 8 p.m. and 10 p.m., says Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: To prevent excessive air and noise pollution during the Deepavali festival, the Karnataka government has issued a slew of instructions to officials, including restricting cracker bursting hours from 8 p.m. to 10 p.m., and also filing criminal cases against vendors who are in possession of banned non-green crackers.

In a directive to the officials, Minister for Forest, Environment and Ecology Ramalinga Reddy said that only green crackers should be allowed and that they should be authenticated through emblem and QR code. Bursting of crackers will not be allowed near hospitals, educational institutions, and other prohibited areas, he said.

The Minister said that Deputy Commissioners of districts should form squads comprising both officials and non-officials to inspect the godowns of firecracker vendors and seize the stock if they sell non-green varieties. He instructed officials to create public awareness about eco-friendly way of celebrating Deepavali through pamphlets and hoardings at public places.

He asked the officials to focus on scientific disposal of cracker waste collected during the festival. He said illegal transportation of banned crackers from other States should be confiscated along with the vehicles.

Pointing out that both the Supreme Court and High Court had issued directives on preventing environmental hazards during bursting of crackers, he asked the Deputy Commissioners, Superintendents of Police, and Commissioners of local bodies to bring the directives to the notice of officials for effective implementation.

articles.title: Free child-care training programme for women in Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Sri Sathya Sai Seva Organisations, Visakhapatnam district, in association with the Andhra Pradesh State Skill Development Corporation (APSSDC), will offer free child-care training to women aged 19 to 40 from November 2.
The 360-hour programme will be conducted at the Sri Sathya Sai Mahila Skill Development Centre in Yendada. Women who have passed or failed Class 10 are eligible to enrol.

According to the organisers, participants who complete the training will receive a government certificate. The programme aims to equip them with skills to pursue employment in child-care centres, hospitals, and kindergartens, or take up home-based child-care services.

articles.title: Man, accused of secretly filming woman on Namma Metro, questioned
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A 38-year-old man accused of secretly filming a woman passenger on Bengaluru’s Namma Metro was questioned by the Bengaluru police, who have seized his mobile phone for forensic examination.

According to the police, the accused, Santosh, denied the allegations and recorded his statement with the Kadugodi police on October 29. The police said that Santosh resides in Nagarabhavi and travels to Whitefield, where he works at a private company. The alleged filming took place near Pattandur Agrahara Metro Station. The police have conducted mahazar at the metro station.
A police officer investigating the case told The Hindu that the accused had obtained anticipatory bail but had been directed by the magistrate to cooperate with the investigation.
“We questioned him and asked about the video, and he showed us that there was no such video on his mobile phone. We will summon him again once the reports arrive,” the officer said.

The case came to light after the woman took to social media to recount the incident. Subsequently, a complaint was lodged. The accused has been booked under Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with stalking.

articles.title: Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia named next IAF Vice Chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Air Marshal Walia headed the Directorate of Air Staff Inspection (DASI) of the IAF, served as the defence attache at Indian embassies in Japan and South Korea, and was the Senior Air Staff Officer of Eastern Air Command.
Air Marshal Inderpal Singh Walia will be the next Vice Chief of the Air Staff, the Defence Ministry announced on Friday (October 30, 2026).
He will succeed incumbent Vice Chief Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who will take charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on Saturday.
Air Marshal Walia is currently serving as the Air Officer Commanding-in-Chief of the Eastern Air Command.
The officer is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy and was commissioned in the fighter stream of the Indian Air Force (IAF) on June 11, 1988.
He is qualified on all variants of the MiG-21, MiG-23, MiG-27, Jaguar and Su-30 MKI jets.
In a career spanning almost four decades, Air Marshal Walia has tenanted various command and staff appointments.
He has commanded a frontline fighter squadron, the Tactics and Air Combat Development Establishment (TACDE) and was Air Officer Commanding of Air Force Station Bareilly.
He has undergone the advanced command and staff course in the U.K..

Air Marshal Walia also headed the Directorate of Air Staff Inspection (DASI) of the IAF, served as the defence attache at Indian embassies in Japan and South Korea, and was the Senior Air Staff Officer of Eastern Air Command.
He holds three Post-Graduate degrees in Defence and Strategic studies.
In recognition of his distinguished service, he was awarded the Vayu Sena Medal in 2008 and Ati Vishisht Seva Medal in 2018.

articles.title: Kavitha blames BRS, Congress for Adilabad’s irrigation woes; accuses BJP of neglecting CCI plant revival
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Telangana Rakshana Sena (TRS) president K. Kavitha alleged that Adilabad district remained deprived of irrigation facilities despite the Godavari and Pranahita rivers flowing through the region. She accused the previous BRS and the present Congress governments of neglecting the district.

Addressing a public meeting titled ‘Panchajanya Sankalpa Sabha’ at Indervelli in Adilabad district on Friday evening, she criticised Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy for holding talks with Maharashtra Chief Minister after ‘considerable delay’ even as farmers were staring at drought. Mr. Revanth Reddy owes farmers an explanation on when the project would be taken up, she said.

She also accused Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K.T. Rama Rao of failing to establish a textile park in Adilabad despite the district producing around 80 lakh quintals of cotton during his tenure as Industries Minister in the past.

Blaming the BRS, Congress and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) for failing to revive the defunct Cement Corporation of India (CCI) plant in Adilabad, she accused the three parties of betraying the people of Adilabad district.
Ms. Kavitha said her party had announced BC candidates for the forthcoming Graduate MLC elections in both constituencies, demonstrating its commitment to social justice.

articles.title: Disinvestment as key economic strategy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Given the fact that privatisation of several PSEs is a long journey, calibrated disinvestment could serve as an interim measure

S even months into 2026-27, the fiscal year has been shaped by global uncertainty, high energy prices and worries over a deficient monsoon. Against this backdrop, disinvestment and asset monetisation have helped in navigating a challenging fiscal year. While receipts were already on course to meet the budget target, the government’s approval of the sale of its share in the IDBI Bank on October 14 makes it likely that the target will be exceeded. For the industry and investors, the receipts are a signal of the government’s continued commitment to reforms and a larger role for the private sector. This year so far, the disinvestment trajectory has progressed well, even before the IDBI stake sale. According to DIPAM data, the Centre mobilised ₹62,124 crore in April-September 2026 through disinvestment and asset monetisation, of which ₹55,757 crore came from disinvestment. These collections had already reached 78% of the full-year budget target of ₹80,000 crore. With the IDBI proceeds, the collections are to head past the target.

This comes at a time when the government looks to diversify its revenue sources amid rising expenditure commitments. Net tax revenue rose by a modest 3.4% in April-August 2026 and non-tax revenue by 3.2%, while capital expenditure was up by over 18%. Overall, the fiscal deficit has already reached 42% of the budgeted levels which implies a tight balance between revenue shortfalls and spending risks.

articles.title: Ukraine has resumed strikes on Russian oil refineries, Russia says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: There was no immediate comment from Ukraine
Ukraine has resumed its attacks on Russian oil refineries after a brief pause, Russia's deputy prime minister said Friday, warning the strikes could reduce Moscow's planned diesel exports.
U.S. President Donald Trump had been pressuring Kyiv for weeks to stop such attacks, blaming them for the rising cost of diesel.
Analysts have linked rising fuel prices to the war the United States and Israel launched against Iran in February.

"There was an attack overnight on Russian oil-processing facilities... specifically, three oil refineries and one gas-chemical complex," Russia's deputy prime minister for energy issues, Alexander Novak, told a reporter from state TV.
"We had a lull that lasted a certain time, but today the attacks on oil refineries resumed," he added.

Videos published by Russian Telegram channels purported to show smoke billowing from an oil refinery in Russia's Samara region -- located 800 kilometres from the Ukrainian border -- following a drone attack overnight.
Regional governor Vyacheslav Fedorishchev said on Telegram that two men had been killed in a Ukrainian drone strike.
Kyiv has repeatedly struck Russian oil and gas sites in retaliation for Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure since Moscow began its offensive there in February 2022.
Mr. Trump, earlier in October, struck an agreement with Russia's President Vladimir Putin to ease sanctions on Moscow in exchange for it releasing diesel onto global markets.

Following the deal, which sparked an outcry from Kyiv and Ukraine's European allies, Mr. Trump announced a surprise "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine, which Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky said he knew nothing about.

Mr. Trump's sanctions deal was seen as an effort to drive prices down in the United States, which consumes approximately 3.9 million barrels of diesel each day, ahead of next week's midterm elections.

Mr. Novak said on Friday (October 30, 2026) that Russia had shipped around 510,000 tonnes of diesel to global markets under the deal in October, adding that "we are planning for a higher amount in November", or around 2.15 million tonnes.

articles.title: Independent Russian newspaper Novaya Gazeta shuts under Kremlin pressure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The closure of Novaya Gazeta — one of the last outlets to openly criticise Russia's offensive — marks a new low in Moscow's campaign against dissenting voices that gained speed after the Kremlin sent troops into its neighbour in 2022

Russia's flagship independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced on Friday (October 30, 2026) it was closing, saying it had been "killed" by State pressure after years of repression targeting its journalists whose reporting was critical of the Kremlin and its Ukraine war.

The closure of Novaya Gazeta — one of the last outlets to openly criticise Russia's offensive — marks a new low in Moscow's campaign against dissenting voices that gained speed after the Kremlin sent troops into its neighbour in 2022.

Since then, the newspaper, long considered a bastion of independent journalism, has seen its media license revoked, while its journalists and editors have been questioned, detained and had their homes searched.
It was also branded a "foreign agent" — a label reminiscent of Soviet-era repression used to stifle dissent.
The paper's Nobel Prize-winning founder, Dmitry Muratov, told AFP the closure was "part of a giant military campaign being waged by the Russian Federation".
"We are fierce opponents of war in all its forms. And we are a part that needed to be destroyed," Mr. Muratov, the paper's former editor-in-chief, said.
Novaya Gazeta's current editor-in-chief, Sergei Sokolov, said the paper was "ending its existence" in a statement published on YouTube on Friday (October 30, 2026) morning.
In the emotional video, Mr. Sokolov said that "the Russian authorities — the Russian special services — have forced the editorial team to end its work."
Founded in 1993 after the collapse of the Soviet Union, Novaya Gazeta was one of Russia's most reputable and renowned organisations reporting and documenting human rights abuses.
Mikhail Gorbachev, the last leader of the Soviet Union, donated some of his Nobel Peace Prize money to help set up the paper.

" Novaya Gazeta has announced that it is ceasing its activities, but Novaya Gazeta will never stop inspiring us. We are Novaya Gazeta ," Reporters Without Borders chief, Thibaut Bruttin, said on Friday (October 30, 2026).
" Novaya Gazeta will remain the symbol of free, pluralistic, independent, and rigorous journalism — a model for the entire profession around the world," he added.

articles.title: China denies spying on Nvidia's Jensen Huang
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips, designed by industry leader Nvidia and used to train and run AI models
Beijing dismissed as "groundless speculation" on Friday (October 30, 2026) a report that said Jensen Huang, head of U.S. chip giant Nvidia, was the target of a Chinese spy plot.

The article by The New York Times , published on Thursday (October 29, 2026), said that U.S. intelligence officials concluded that a Chinese executive linked to a Singapore-based data centre company had been funnelling information to Beijing.
"The report in question is based on groundless speculation and is nothing more than an attempt to smear China," Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing.

China is in a race for tech dominance with the United States, which restricts the export to China of the most cutting-edge silicon chips, designed by industry leader Nvidia and used to train and run AI models.
The data centre company, Megaspeed, was under scrutiny for possibly steering Nvidia AI chips to China, the report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the matter.
But the executive Alice Huang — also known as Huang Le, and no relation to 63-year-old Taiwanese-born Jensen Huang — developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the New York Times said.
That could have given her insights into U.S. President Donald Trump's thinking around AI, an issue likely to arise during talks with China's President Xi Jinping next month.
Mr. Trump was briefed on the intelligence findings roughly a year ago and chose not to act on the information, the report said.
Nvidia is the world's most valuable company thanks to the global drive to build data centres packed with specialist computer chips and other hardware that runs AI systems.
An Nvidia spokesperson told AFP on Friday (October 30, 2026) that Megaspeed was like any other regional customer and "Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected".
"Our regional cloud customers receive ordinary business information — not sensitive NVIDIA trade secrets — and zero information relevant to national security," they said.
The spokesperson added that allegations the Singaporean company was smuggling chips to China "were thoroughly investigated and debunked last year".

articles.title: China ruling party says 'eliminated dangers' after 33 expelled
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: In more than a decade in charge, Xi has cracked down hard on graft, ensnaring thousands of officials and purging dozens of members of the powerful Central Committee and a string of top military brass

China has eradicated "serious hidden dangers" in its Communist Party and military under President Xi Jinping's leadership, a senior official said on Friday (October 30, 2026), a day after authorities confirmed the expulsion of a record 33 figures.

articles.title: Thousands of students, workers protest in Italy under heavy security
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Marches were held in dozens of cities up and down the country, including in Bologna, Genoa, Naples, and Turin — where a few minor skirmishes between protesters and riot police occurred at the start of the protest

Thousands of students and workers took to the streets across Italy on Friday (October 30, 2026), calling for more school funding and relief from the soaring cost of living, amid a high police presence to avert possible clashes.

Friday's (October 30, 2026) Italy-wide protest comes after weeks of demonstrations, led by students who have set up tent camps and occupied schools to make their demands heard, fuelled by similar movements in nearby France and Spain.

A general strike called by Italy's USB trade union attracted thousands of workers to Friday's (October 30, 2026) protests, including truck drivers, taxi drivers, and farmers who have rallied in recent weeks over the spike in fuel prices and to oppose rising defence spending.

Marches were held in dozens of cities up and down the country, including in Bologna, Genoa, Naples, and Turin — where a few minor skirmishes between protesters and riot police occurred at the start of the protest.
In Rome, university student Beatrice Chilelli told AFP students were "at a breaking point".

"They can't afford to pay exorbitant tuition fees, and rent... which weighs heavily on their parents' shoulders," said the 21-year-old, citing student housing in Rome that could reach 1,200 euros per month for a single room.

Thousands of people left Rome's central Termini train station, accompanied by two tractors and a taxi, making their way past the Colosseum as they waved flags, unfurled banners and shouted into megaphones.
An AFP photographer witnessed a heavy police presence outside the Economy Ministry, which the procession passed by.
"We need more houses, not bombs!" sang one group in the crowd, as a troupe of protesters gave a brief performance imitating terrified civilians in a Gaza bombing raid.

The Milan protest also began at the central train station, but then headed outside the city — far from the centre where young vandals had looted stores, destroyed property, and clashed with police two weeks ago after another sanctioned cost-of-living demonstration.
"Let's reclaim our future" read one banner unfurled by students in Milan.
Police in riot gear blocked off streets, but no major clashes had been reported as of midday.

articles.title: India orders Sun Pharma to halt eye-care drug production at plant after quality lapses
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: India’s drug quality standards have come under increased scrutiny at home and overseas in recent years after locally made cough syrups were linked to ‌the deaths of children in India and also in countries including Gambia and Uzbekistan

Indian drug regulators ordered Sun Pharmaceutical Industries to stop manufacturing, selling and distributing ophthalmic products made at its Assam facility after finding ‌failure in its quality management system, documents reviewed by Reuters showed.

The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation and ​the office of Drugs Controller Assam ordered the shutdown on August 20 after a joint federal-state inspection of ⁠the facility identified lapses in the system meant to ensure product quality and safety, following Sun Pharma’s move in July to voluntarily recall about 11 eye-care brands.

India’s drug quality standards have come under increased scrutiny at home and overseas in recent years after locally made cough syrups were linked to ‌the deaths of children in India and also in countries including Gambia and Uzbekistan.

The regulatory agencies’ move marks an escalation of the action against Sun Pharma, India’s biggest pharmaceutical firm, which will be unable to continue ophthalmic drug ‌production at the Assam factory until it submits a satisfactory compliance report. Sun Pharma said previously the site was expected ‌to become ⁠one of its largest manufacturing hubs for sterile products in a business identified as a key global growth ⁠driver.
The regulator sought more information on the recall of 332 batches of ophthalmic suspension products — liquids used to treat eye conditions — the documents showed.

In an internal notice sent to stockists at the time, the company said it was withdrawing the products as a “precautionary measure.” It remains unclear whether all of the recalled products were ​contaminated.
Sun Pharma did not publicly disclose details of ‌the recall.

The company has submitted a compliance report in response to the order, which is being reviewed by the regulator, an official familiar with the matter told Reuters on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak to the media.

“We voluntarily initiated a temporary cessation of manufacturing activities and informed the regulators,” Sun Pharma said in a statement on Friday (October 30, 2026), ‌adding that remedial measures have been put in place.
It did not respond to a request for comment on the ​recall. The company says on its website it follows a single global quality standard.

Some of the recalled products included Lotepred 1% 5ml eye drops, Nepalact OD eye drops, ⁠Nepalact-Z, Brinzotim eye drops 5ml and Depopred 2ml. The eye drops are used to treat eye inflammation, infections and chronic eye diseases, according to doctors.
It is unclear whether these eye products were exported from India or whether any patients reported any adverse effects.

articles.title: Two held over death of cheetah; firearm as yet untraced
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Two people have been arrested in connection with the killing of a male cheetah cub at the Kuno National Park, officials said on Friday (October 30, 2026).

A senior wildlife official told The Hindu that two people had been arrested after questioning. “The arrest has been made by a special task force formed for the purpose under the Arms Act, after which the accused were produced before a court. They are currently in police remand, and we will take custody soon,” the official said, requesting anonymity.

“The case will be solved very soon, and we will reveal everything in a day or two. At the moment, multiple teams are at work,” the official said adding that more than five forest personnel had been suspended.

Another senior wildlife official, however, said that the two persons had been detained on Thursday (October 29) evening while the weapon, believed to be a country-made bharmar gun, is yet to be recovered.

“Several people in villages near the spot where the cub was found have been questioned so far and based on that two locals were detained last night [Thursday]. They were arrested today. Searches have also been conducted in the area to find the gun,” the official said, adding that the accused were being questioned about the circumstances of the incident and the firearm used.
Earlier on Thursday (October 29), officials had said that investigating teams have been scanning a large area, mapping the cub’s movement over 15-20 days based on its tracking radio-collar.
The probe is being led by a four-member special task force formed by the State Government along with the State Tiger Strike Force

Officials suspect that the weapon used in the shooting is “a country-made bharmar gun”, a traditional single-shot, muzzle-loading smoothbore firearm that is popular is the rural and forest parts of the region.

The 19-month-old cub, KNG22, an offspring of South African cheetah Nirva, had been found with five gunshot injuries in Sheopur forest division on October 25 and died during treatment on October 27 in Jabalpur. This was the first instance of a cheetah being shot since Project Cheetah, a reintroduction programme for the species, was launched in September, 2022.

articles.title: Infosys opens 1.1 million sq.ft. new block at Pocharam campus in Hyderabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The new facility will add 10,000 seats, enabling the company to aim to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model, the IT major said after the inauguration by Deputy CM Bhatti, IT Minister Sridhar Babu
IT major Infosys announced expansion of its Pocharam Development Centre in Hyderabad with the inauguration of a 1.1 million sq.ft. software development block on Friday.

Spread across 450 acres, its campus in Pocharam currently houses seven software development blocks with approximately 4.58 million sq.ft. of built-up area. The new block will add 10,000 seats, enabling the company to aim to support an additional workforce of over 13,000 employees under a hybrid working model, Infosys said after the inauguration in which Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka, IT and Industries Minister D.Sridhar Babu participated.

The expansion of the Pocharam campus by Infosys marks another important milestone for Telangana, which has established itself as a global technology destination, supported by world-class infrastructure, skilled talent and a thriving innovation ecosystem, the Deputy CM said.

“Investments of this scale reinforce Hyderabad’s position as a preferred destination for global enterprises and advance our vision of a future-ready, innovation-driven economy,” he was quoted in a release issued by Infosys. The expansion of the facility will create opportunities for the youth to participate in the next wave of technology-led growth, said Mr.Vikramarka, who is also Minister for Finance, Planning and Energy.

The Pocharam Development Centre supports global clients across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), retail, Life Sciences and manufacturing. The expansion will further strengthen the company’s capabilities in AI, Cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and next-generation digital services, Infosys said, without sharing investment on the new facility.

Chief Financial Officer of Infosys Jayesh Sanghrajka said Hyderabad has played a pivotal role in the company’s growth and the expansion of the Pocharam campus reflects its continued commitment to the region.

“The facility enhances our capacity to scale operations, build specialised talent and deliver complex transformation programmes for global clients. As enterprises accelerate adoption of AI, the campus will serve as a strategic hub bringing together world-class talent, advanced infrastructure and deep capabilities to help clients drive innovation...”, he said.

On the features of the new facility, Infosys said it incorporates energy-efficient radiant cooling, smart lighting, rainwater harvesting, wastewater reuse and natural daylight-filled spaces. It also features flexible workspaces, collaborative areas and employee wellness facilities to support a modern, hybrid work environment.

IT major Infosys announced expansion of its Pocharam Development Centre in Hyderabad with the inauguration of a 1.1 million sq.ft. software development block on Friday.

Spread across 450 acres, its campus in Pocharam currently houses seven software development blocks with approximately 4.58 million sq.ft. of built-up area. The expansion of the Pocharam campus by Infosys marks another important milestone for Telangana, which has established itself as a global technology destination, supported by world-class infrastructure, skilled talent and a thriving innovation ecosystem, the Deputy CM said.

“Investments of this scale reinforce Hyderabad’s position as a preferred destination for global enterprises and advance our vision of a future-ready, innovation-driven economy,” he was quoted in a release issued by Infosys. The expansion of the facility will create opportunities for the youth to participate in the next wave of technology-led growth, said Mr.Vikramarka, who is also Minister for Finance, Planning and Energy.

The Pocharam Development Centre supports global clients across banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI), retail, Life Sciences and manufacturing. The expansion will further strengthen the company’s capabilities in AI, Cloud, cybersecurity, engineering and next-generation digital services, Infosys said, without sharing investment on the new facility.

articles.title: Will not enforce circular on hospital medicine price disclosure for now: Karnataka government to HC
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The circular mandates that all hospital pharmacies disclose the landing base/purchase price and maximum retail price of medicines, medical devices and consumables on bills.

The State government on Friday (October 30) told the Karnataka High Court that it would not insist, for now, on the implementation of the circular which mandates that all hospital pharmacies disclose the landing base/purchase price and maximum retail price (MRP) of medicines, medical devices and consumables on bills.

An undertaking in this regard was given to the court on behalf of the State’s Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) during the hearing of a petition filed by Private Hospitals and Nursing Homes Association, Bengaluru, and a private hospital. The petitioners have challenged the legality of the October 1 circular.

Justice C.M. Pooncha, before whom the petition came up for hearing, has adjourned further hearing on the petition till November 11 after recording the undertaking given by an Additional Advocate General on instruction from the officials of the FSDA.

The government also informed the court that “the officials concerned are in the process of having a re-look at the circular dated October 1, 2026, and will not enforce the mandate of the circular till November 11, the next date of hearing on the petition”.
The undertaking was given while requesting the court not to stay the circular to allow the government to re-examine the issues raised by the petitioners.

It was contended on behalf of the petitioners that the FSDA had no statutory power to impose such conditions for disclosure of purchase price, which is a commercial agreement between the sellers and buyers that vary depending on suppliers, purchase quantity, discounts, credit arrangements and other factors.

Mandating disclosure of purchase price would result in exposing confidential commercial arrangements between the suppliers and health establishments, it has been contented in the petition, while pointing out that the circular was issued sans adequate consultations with the stakeholders, even though the circular has direct implications on their finance.

articles.title: Quantum tech can help solve complex problems: Jnan Yalla
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Qiskit Fall Fest inaugurated at Visvesvaraya Technological University in Belagavi

“Quantum computing is not merely the next step in computer technology. It is a technology that can bring about a significant transformation in our ability to solve complex problems,” according to Research Officer in the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Central government Jnan Yalla.
He was speaking after inaugurating the Qiskit Fall Fest organised by Visvesvaraya Technological University (VTU) in association with IBM on Jnana Sangama in Belagavi on Friday.

“Quantum technology will open up immense opportunities in the fields of healthcare, drug discovery, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, climate change and the development of new material. India is also taking significant steps towards strengthening its research and development capabilities in the field of quantum technology,” he said.

“As engineering students, you should not look at this technology merely as a subject but consider it an opportunity to shape the future. You have the potential to gain global recognition through innovative ideas, a research-oriented mindset and continuous learning,” he told students.
VTU Vice-Chancellor S. Vidyashankar urged students to cultivate curiosity and undertake research with determination.

“Everyone should work together to create something new and shape tomorrow’s technology. We are organising such conferences to introduce students to quantum technology, which is a technology of the future, and to encourage them to study it in depth. Students should make the best use of these opportunities,” he said.

“Quantum computing has the potential to bring about significant changes in future technology. In particular, quantum algorithms offer new opportunities to make artificial intelligence and machine learning processes faster and more efficient,” IBM Engineer A. Janani said.
As part of the programme, students were given opportunities to find solutions to problems through poster presentations and a hackathon.
Several technical sessions were also held. A report on the activities of the Quantum Club was released.
Registrar (Evaluation) U.J. Ujwal, faculty member Harish Bendigeri, VTU Quantum Club Student Chair Karthik Rao and others were present.
